FOUR WAGE TUESDAYS FALL IN THIS BATCH AND TWO OF THEM WERE NOT PAID.**

### 3. FOUR FIGURES THE CHAPTERS DECIDED, AND THE FIGURE IN THE PROMPT THAT IS CORRECTED TO THEM

**THE WEEK OF TUESDAY THE FIFTH OF SEPTEMBER WAS NOT PAID AND THE PROMPT'S FIGURE OF *ONE WEEK FALLEN DUE WITH NO ENVELOPE* IS CORRECTED TO TWO.** `state/current.md`'s money table for Batch 0001 records the chain across the first to the tenth of September as *nothing in*, and that is decisive: the bag stood at a mark and twelve shillings and fourpence on the morning of the fifth and four marks was not in it. **Chapter 161 therefore enters the week of Tuesday the fifth of September as unpaid, on the twelfth and not before, with the reason against the line, and says plainly that the party did not enter it on the fifth and why — that a party which begins to enter a wage late and then enters it on a day of its own choosing is a party whose column has stopped being a column and become a diary.** The count of envelopes on the bench is **thirteen** on the twelfth, **fourteen** on the nineteenth and **fifteen** on the twenty-sixth, and the number of weeks fallen due this year with no envelope standing against them is **two**, being the fifteenth of August and the fifth of September, entered in the same breath in every place it is given, because an envelope that is not made is not a wage and this column is not the wage. **THE FIFTEENTH OF AUGUST STAYS UNPAID AND THE FIFTH OF SEPTEMBER IS NEW, AND NEITHER IS PAID IN THIS BATCH AND NEITHER IS ENTERED TWICE.**

**THE OTHER THREE: the wage of Tuesday the twelfth was not paid and the envelope was not made; the wages of the nineteenth and the twenty-sixth were paid; and the bag closes the month on the figure it opened it on, because two days of work paid two wages and the two unpaid weeks were neither paid nor made better.** A day at the second seam's own face brought **three** on the fourteenth and **five** on the twenty-second, and neither is argued on the mole's steps and the eighth and the share come off the top of both the way they have come off the top of every day rate since the third of May.

### 4. Every document and instrument created, quoted, or discovered in this batch

1. **A direction of a sitting**, read out in the hearing room over the tide-gang store on **Saturday the sixteenth of September at ten in the morning**, by **Ambrose Sell, clerk of the circuit office and clerk of that sitting**: that the inquiry stands directed to a sitting to be appointed, to be held at that room **in the week following the twelfth day of October next**, and that a paper naming the day will be served on the party and not left with anybody; that the party may apply in writing, **at its own cost**, for a copy of any record produced or referred to at any sitting, and that the direction grants no copy and makes none and releases nothing and no date attaches to any of it, and that whether any office in any city has any intention of doing any of it is not a fact and is not given to the party; and that the construction of the second paragraph of the notice of the tenth stands, and that nothing in the direction touches, grants, refuses or deals with the second season of the said writ. **The clerk also said, in three things that are not on the paper, that the power to seat one of two disputants is in the notice and is NOT THE WRIT'S POWER and did not come out of the writ, and that a record in a city is in a file and was not in that room and he would not say what is in it and would not say why.**
2. **A form of four sentences** in Calder Marr's own left hand, put on the table face up on the sixteenth and **not read out**: that no finding of worked glass, whole or in part, was made on or about Tuesday the eighth of August by this party or by anybody in its boat; that nothing was raised on that day; that no return has gone up on that day and none is going to; and that the party will produce its crew's book whole and unshortened at any sitting, and that a copy of it is already in a file in a city and this party has entered that and cannot stop it. **A form and not a return, and not a conclusion and not a confession, and the party said so out loud.**
3. **The crew's book produced a second time, whole and unshortened, in about nine minutes, and NOT ONE LINE OF IT READ ALOUD, and no copy of it made in that room.** The writ, face down. The four returns, in order, with the days against them. The sheet of the twenty-fifth of August with a copy of it, which the yard made itself. And the party's own first-column line for the eighth of August, handed over whole, unshortened, and not read out. **All six items of the fourth paragraph were produced, two of them are the same line, and one whole item of the list is a line saying that there is no finding at all.**
4. **A printed sheet, bought off a stall in a counting office in a city for a penny on the morning of Friday the twenty-second**, being a setting in type of the yard's own sheet of the twenty-fifth of August or of a copy of it, carrying at its head the name of a printer in a city and a date and nothing else, and carrying **this yard's two and three-quarters and the other man's two and a half side by side with the words *we are not guessing* between them, and both halves of the sentence about roads, in type, without leave.** **A copy of the yard's own sheet went up this coast in a boat in the ordinary way, and neither figure is withdrawn and neither is going to be, and this volume does not decide which of them is right and this party is not going to decide it in a shed.**
5. **A report of a marine surveyor of a city**, **Ailsa Rorke, surveyor. Fourteen Wharf**, carried in a coat pocket and read out in the yard on Monday the twenty-fifth in about four minutes: that a coaster of about a hundred and ninety tons did not enter the harbor on the morning of the second of August; that the ground is barred to two and three-quarter fathoms at the middle of a spring tide; that a vessel of that draught could not have crossed that ground at twenty past two without taking the ground; **that the surveyor has applied in writing to this party for the figure and has had no answer, and records this party as declining to certify the figure, and records on the face of that entry that she has not had it from this party and has it from a man of the first lay who crossed the water to tell her so**; and that he could not verify the figure, and that the vessel is not his, and that her owner is a man he has not met and cannot meet before Thursday, and that no person in that city can check any figure on the yard's sheet, and that he set out his finding in that uncertainty rather than in another one. **THE DATE CHAIN CLOSES: he wrote to the yard and was not answered, and the man of the first lay told the surveyor in a letter in the first week of September that a yard which has printed a figure of its own cannot be got to swear to it afterwards, and the report was written on the back of that letter and came on the Saturday boat of the nineteenth, and the yard's own refusal is given in a doorway at about half past ten on the Monday the twenty-fifth and is the first refusal anybody made — and that refusal was in a file in a city three days before it was said out loud on a mole.**
6. **A letter from that surveyor**, brought up the hill on Wednesday the twenty-seventh and read out in a doorway, entering: *The yard of Morrow Quay, whose sheet is set in type in this city, gives the bar of that harbor at two and three-quarter fathoms on the flood; declines to certify the figure; and will not be held to it.* **FOUR WORDS IN THAT ENTRY — *will not be held to it* — WERE NEVER SAID BY THIS PARTY, and the surveyor says so in his own letter, and asks whether they are the yard's own words, and says he entered them because a man who will not certify and will not be held to is a man standing behind a figure and does not wish to be examined.** The surveyor is a working man in his trade, has written down the reason he entered what he entered, offered to be wrong in a document rather than vague in one, and is not a villain and is not an antagonist and is not on any ladder.
7. **An undertaking, priced and refused.** In the market office on Friday the twenty-ninth, at about ten past ten, in eleven people's hearing, Calder Marr asked a person of no office for one line in her own trade's words, with her name on it and her price on it, saying what a lump of green glass off a mole's face is and what a chip of worked glass is, and whether the two of them are the same thing. **She priced it before she answered it. THE PRICE IS NOT SIX MARKS AND TWO DAYS AND IS NOT MONEY: it is an undertaking, in this yard's own first column, in the holder's own left hand, with a date on it, that this party does not ask her for anything again — not at a figure, not at nothing, not for a line, not for a name, not in a room and not in a shed.** **The reason she gave is in her own words: a conservator this party cannot pay is a conservator this party has to keep asking, and asking her to be useful is asking her to be cheap; and in about two years, or three, a page in a city with a trade on it has a name on the trade, and then somebody in a room says *the conservator* and means a woman and not a trade. THE ANSWER WAS NO, AND NO MONEY CHANGED HANDS, AND NO SHEET WAS ASKED FOR AT THE PRESS AND NO SHILLING WAS PAID.**
8. **A name, at a woman's own asking, in the first column and not on a wall.** Sella Brigg, eight shillings and tenpence, undiminished, unpaid, entered on Sunday the twenty-fourth with the hour against it, **at her request and with her name on it, and she came up the hill to say she is not going to be a name on the yard's public sheet and that if a name goes on it she will take her own warp off it in front of people.**
9. **A paper of a refused license**, folded in two in the back of the writ of the first of May, brought out on Saturday the twenty-third: nine sentences in Calder Marr's own left hand refusing thirty marks in coin for a license to go and look at a road. **It is not re-decided, it is not argued, and the reason it came out of the book is that a bag with twelve shillings and fourpence in it is the only kind of afternoon that puts a man's hand on a thing he has not touched since the third of May.**
10. **FIRST-COLUMN ENTRIES AND SECOND-COLUMN ENTRIES, COUNTED AGAIN BY HAND ON THE ITALIC ENTRY PARAGRAPHS AFTER THE BATCH'S REVIEW REPAIRS, WITH THE METHOD GIVEN BECAUSE THE NEXT BATCH INHERITS IT AND HAS TO BE ABLE TO RECOUNT IT.** **The earlier figure in this section — first-column *2 · 2 · 3 · 2 · 2 · 2 · 2 · 3 · 2 · 2* and second-column *1 · 1 · 2 · 2 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 2*, being 22 and 13 — WAS WRONG AND IS WITHDRAWN. IT COUNTED THE CONTINUATION PARAGRAPHS OF AN ENTRY AS ENTRIES OF THEIR OWN.** The verified count is **first-column 2 · 1 · 2 · 2 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1 = THIRTEEN ENTRIES, and second-column 1 · 1 · 2 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1 = ELEVEN ENTRIES**, being **thirteen and eleven**, against seventeen and six in Batch 0001. **There are twenty-one further italic paragraphs that continue an entry already begun, and they are not separate entries: 2 · 3 · 0 · 2 · 2 · 3 · 1 · 3 · 2 · 3.** The method, so that the next volume can recount it: an entry is an italic paragraph beginning *First column* or *Second column*; **a paragraph beginning *And that* is the continuation of the entry above it and belongs to whichever column that entry is in.** **A machine count of the words *Second column* across the ten chapters now returns ELEVEN, which is the true number, and it used to be held against this file as evidence that two of the entries did not open with those words; they all do.** The proportion note in the reviewer's craft list stands and is a fact about the batch's shape and not a defect in any chapter: **thirteen first-column entries and eleven second-column entries across ten chapters, and the two-column practice is this yard's written practice and is lock L21.**

### 5. The dated positions at the end of Chapter 170

- **The writ.** Granted Monday the first of May, running to midnight on the first of March next, not the Second Bell license, not a charter, renewing nothing, ground not widened, four names and no fifth. **The second season is still a named absence and nothing in this batch touches, grants, refuses or deals with it.**
- **The notice of the thirty-first of October.** Not lifted, not narrowed, not re-served, not altered; the harbor authority has no power to lift it. **NO PERSON, NO BOAT AND NO LEAD OF THIS YARD WAS INSIDE THE FIRST CLAUSE ON ANY DAY OF THIS BATCH, and this is entered in the first column in Chapter 162 with the date.** **The two objects of nobody's on the crown: a hundred and seventeen days on the eleventh of September, about a hundred and twenty-four on the eighteenth, about a hundred and twenty-six on the twentieth, and about a hundred and thirty-six days at the close of the thirtieth, and NEITHER OBJECT HAS MOVED and one tarpaulin still has a corner off it since the seventeenth of June.**
- **The acknowledgements: eight, the ninth entered on the twenty-eighth of August by this party, and the tenth may not be entered. THIS BATCH ENTERED NONE, ASKED FOR NONE, AND RECORDED IN THE FIRST COLUMN ON THE TWELFTH THAT IT DID NOT GO AND DID NOT ASK, AND WHY.**
- **The plate at the fifth seam is in eleven feet, seen and not measured and not touched, and the eight-clause plan of the seventeenth of January is refused in a record with a date on it. The plate note IS OPEN AND THE CHAPTERS SAY SO. THE REMOVED FILE PAGE AND THE DOCUMENT ARE RESERVED TO MOVEMENT 3 AND WERE NOT PRODUCED, QUOTED, SUMMARIZED OR DESCRIBED IN THIS BATCH, INCLUDING SAYING THAT ONE HAPPENED.**
- **The bell is off the south end in eight and a half feet and is not going out and is not going to go out inside four years. NO BOAT WENT OFF THE SOUTH END IN THIS BATCH, NO SECOND EIGHT MARKS WAS ENTERED AS PAID, THE BELLWRIGHT WAS NOT ASKED AND IS IN NO CHAPTER OF IT AS A PERSON, AND THE CHEST WAS NOT OPENED AND WAS NOT BROUGHT DOWN THE HILL.**
- **The lead plug. Not asked about, not printed, not opened, and not brought down the hill.** The undertaking of the second of July binds the yard and not the office and not the market and not the boy.
- **THE CONDITION IS NAMED ONCE IN THIS BATCH, IN CHAPTER 164, ON LAND, IN A DOORWAY, IN THE SECOND COLUMN, IN THE HOLDER'S OWN LEFT HAND, WITH A REASON AGAINST THE LINE.** The bare fact: *the holder cannot always tell which of two things he said in the last minute was the one he had decided to say, and it happened on a Sunday afternoon in a doorway to a man of the third lay who came up a hill in the rain to say where a boy was, and the holder was not in the water and has not been in the water since the eighth of August, and this is a tide-sickness and has been got since the fourteenth of October of last year and is not going off.* **The four lines above the named line of the twentieth of July are still four, are still nameless, and are not struck out, and the count of four stands in the first column in a ship's hand with no name against it. THE ONE NAMING VOLUME 04 WAS ALLOWED IS NOW SPENT AND IS NOT AVAILABLE AGAIN IN THIS VOLUME OR ANY OTHER.**
- **The glass storm.** Not used. No cause is named for it in this batch or in any volume, and nothing in either line knows anything.
- **The coast road.** Described, published, doubted, printed in a city, and **not resolved and not called anything by anybody in this batch.** Both figures for the bar of gravel are in type in a city, side by side, and neither is withdrawn and this volume does not decide which is right. **The Kettle was not looked at. Five miles of that coast has not been looked at and is not going to be this season, and that is on the face of the yard's own sheet in the yard's own words. The refused license is carried as a cost and is not re-decided.**
- **The run under this town.** Not explained, not named, not pursued, and not referred to.
- **Custody.** Three items, three numbers, no digit quoted, none returns, none asked for, the municipal claim on the third stands, and **the word does not occur in any of the ten chapters of this batch.**
- **The concealment.** Hidden. The Oren mark is in no record, in no office, in no book and not in the reeve's chart notation.
- **The delayed note.** Eleven logged occasions and two of them with no call in them. **NEITHER COUNT WAS ADVANCED IN THIS BATCH BY ARITHMETIC OR BY A MEASUREMENT. NO OCCASION WAS ENTERED AND NO MEASUREMENT WAS TAKEN AND THE DELAY IS A HAND'S WIDTH OF A SECOND AND HAS NOT MOVED AND NOBODY IN THIS HARBOR HAS EVER SAID WHY.**
- **Labor.** **No air bought in this batch and no hose and no gland paid and no day of work done that wanted one.** Two days of work at a seam, at three and at five. Two wages paid, two not. One herring berth out. The north berth out. The tide gang four men short. **The cistern on a rota of a Monday and a Thursday, charged at no figure on the fourth, seventh, eleventh, fourteenth, eighteenth, twenty-first, twenty-fifth and twenty-eighth of September, which is eight days, and walked by this party on none of the eight.** The mole-head light not on. The fire party's hose dead until the spring. The hard at Ashtide unanswered since the ninth of November. Nineteen winters in a naval file and in a list being made up in a city by an officer this yard emptied, and **nobody in Morrow Quay will ever be able to check what she writes with them.** The *Sea Wren* at the pile, and this party has not thanked him and has not been asked to. Neave Tarrant, nine winters, out since the twenty-eighth of February, not found, one line, and this party has not gone.
- **THE READ-OUT DEVICE WAS USED ONCE IN THIS BATCH AND IT FAILED.** Chapter 168, Monday the twenty-fifth of September, at the head of the dock, in daylight, in about forty people's hearing, the holder read out of the yard's own book the whole of the entry for the bar of gravel — the place, the hour, the lead, the slate, the four times over, the flood and the ebb — together with the reason against the line, and read it twice. **Two men of that market said afterwards to each other that it was the whole of it, and it did nothing whatever for the man it was done for, and the yard entered both halves.** The head-of-dock read-out of a figure and the read-back in the shed are this yard's standing practice and are not uses of the device; **the read-back — the ship's hand reading the day's entries back from the top of the bench and the holder reading them back after her, and nobody else in that shed — runs in FIVE of the ten chapters of this batch, 161, 163, 164, 167 and 170, and Chapter 168 has a variant of it at line 61, where the man who asked for the certification is handed back the line in the second column that belongs to him and is told it was read back to him at nine o'clock that night. CHAPTER 170 DOES NOT OPEN ON IT: it opens on the two words *He went in*, and its read-back is at its seventy-seventh line, out of a hundred and three. The earlier statement in this file that the read-back ran in seven chapters — 161, 163, 164, 165, 166, 168 and 170 — was wrong in both directions and is withdrawn: Chapters 165 and 166 have no read-back and Chapter 167 does.**

### 6. The people, and the four who are not in a room

- **Calder Marr**, thirty-two. **He goes in no water in this batch.** He is on a mole's crown, at a head of a dock, in two doorways, on a bench at a market office, in a hearing room once, and in a shed most nights. **He reads no seam, on a document or on anything else, and the word *faultreader* is on no page of it.** He refused a certification with four reasons, read the figure out at the head of the dock, went into a room he had stood outside of for eighty minutes, was refused, and named the condition once in his own hand in the second column.
- **Nessa Pike**, twenty-seven. The tender, the pump, the fall, the board and the slate, and the standing shutdown. **She won the argument about the second column a second time, on the crown, on Wednesday the thirteenth, in about nine minutes, in nine people's hearing: reasons are long, reasons do not go into a copy, and if the second column is read out in a room then in about four years its five checkless lines are the only thing in forty-seven weeks this yard knew and would not say.** She said the thirty marks were for four hundred feet of a woman's warp, out loud, once. She refused to let the volume's sentence be improved on in a shed. **She did not fill the third column and entered why.** She is the person holding the pencil.
- **Mara Venn**, thirty. **NOT ON THE CREW, NOT ASKED FOR ANYTHING UNTIL THE TWENTY-NINTH, AND PRESENT ON THE TWENTY-NINTH IN A ROOM SHE GOES INTO, WHICH IS OPEN TO ANYBODY ON A FRIDAY MORNING BECAUSE THAT OFFICE IS.** He went in. He asked for one line with her name and her price on it. **She priced it before she answered it, the price is an undertaking and not money, the reason is the volume's own sentence about a conservator this party cannot pay, and the answer is no, and no money changed hands.** Her forty marks stand unpaid, first after food, since the fifteenth of October, and are not reduced. **The six marks and two days are unpaid, unoffered and are not going to be. Her break with the Registry is NOT in this batch, is a different event from her leaving this crew, is Movement 3's beat, and no chapter of this batch shows it, hints at it, or has a character remark that she is not where she was. She did not come back to this crew and is not on it.**
- **Ors Kest**, forty-four. **HE IS IN NO CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH AS A PERSON AND WAS NOT ASKED FOR ANYTHING.** The yard entered in the first column on the twelfth of September that it did not go to the harbor authority and did not ask that office for anything, with the reason. The price of the ninth, a Monday out of a man of the first lay, is unpaid, unthanked and is not going to be said sorry about in a market.
- **Ambrose Sell**, clerk of the circuit office. **NAMED WHEREVER A CLERK OF THE CIRCUIT OFFICE APPEARS, in Chapter 163 only.** He is the clerk of the sitting, said his name and his office before he read the direction, said he was the clerk and not the man who directed it, distinguished the writ's power from the inquiry's power in his own words so that a file in a city does not read them as one, and said that there is a record in a city in a file which was not in that room and that he would not say what is in it and would not say why.
- **The man in a coat is NOT NAMED IN THIS BATCH AND MAY NOT BE NAMED IN THIS VOLUME.** He is in no chapter of it and in no room in it. He is a channel and not a face.
- **Rowan Trewin** does not appear in this batch and is not brought back early. **His visit is spent, he is coming in the spring for nothing, and what is left of him for this batch is a figure in type in a city and a sheet in about sixty boats.**
- **Wil Tranter**, of the first lay, fifty-one, master of a coaster of about two hundred tons. **NEW IN THIS BATCH AND ORDINARY AND NOT A DEVICE.** He bought a printed sheet off a stall for a penny, he crossed the bar on twenty-two springs in nineteen years and put her on it once in the second year, he has a paper of his own and a man in a city asking for his word under a line in it, he wrote to that city on the Monday night without sending this party a copy, he came up the hill on the Wednesday with the answer, and he is the man who says out loud that a man with a page cannot act on a refusal and can act on a name, and that there are three people on this coast who can put a trade at the foot of a line and this yard has none of them. **He is not thanked and does not ask to be, and the yard was not thanked and did not ask to be.**
- **Ailsa Rorke**, a marine surveyor in a city, whose letterhead carries a street and a number and nothing else. **NEW IN THIS BATCH, NAMED, ORDINARY, IN HIS TRADE'S WORDS, AND NOT AN ANTAGONIST.** He is a man with a page who was careful, who wrote down the reason he entered what he entered, who offered to be wrong in a document rather than vague in one, and who asked a question in a letter that is a question and not an accusation.
- **Denzil Hare**, of the third lay, about fifty, a boat of his own. **NEW IN THIS BATCH AND ORDINARY.** He came up the hill in the rain on Sunday the seventeenth and said, unasked and without being asked anything, that the boy was in a fore berth of his from about the sixth to about the twenty-first of June, paid out of his own pocket and not out of a wage, and is not in it and has not been since. **He was not asked one question and he said in the doorway that he had been standing in the yard for four minutes waiting for one.**
- **Tam Rundle**, thirty, of the tide gang, which is four men short. He appears once, on Wednesday the twentieth, with the man of the first lay, and says the figure and the terms and that a day and a half of the gang is the whole of the price and that he is not going to say anything about that either. **Neither of the two of them asked him one word about the nine days he gave on the twenty-ninth of July and neither is going to.**
- **Sella Brigg**, of this harbor, a weaver of warp. **She came up the hill on Sunday the twenty-fourth to say three things and to ask for nothing, and her name and her figure went into the first column at her own asking, and she is not on any wall.**
- **A man of the second lay** who booked a day for the Friday following at his own figure and was told at eight in the morning that the work could not be done, and who said he had known since Tuesday and had come to have it on the yard's book. Unnamed and ordinary.
- **A man of the first lay** of about ninety tons who asked about the ninth seam's mooring and was sent to the tide gang. Unnamed and ordinary.
- **Alden Marr**, sixty-one. **At the far bench on FIVE DAYS OF THIS BATCH — the eleventh, the twelfth, the seventeenth, the eighteenth and the twenty-fourth of September — asked for nothing on any of them, asking nothing, and Calder Marr does not go over to him on any of them, entered in the first column on the eighteenth with the reason: neither brother has said why and neither brother is going to.** No fragment, no report talk, no second story, no confession. **The figure of six days that an earlier draft of this line gave was wrong and matches no chapter; the figure of seven days given in `state/current.md` was wrong twice over, since it added the twenty-ninth and thirtieth, on which no chapter places him at all.**
- **Bevin Rook is in no chapter of this batch as a person** except as a fore berth in June in the mouth of a man of the third lay who was not asked anything. **The three nots stand. The head of the third column keeps his hand. Forty marks stand whole.**
- **Captain Veyra Holt** does not come to this harbor, is not in a room, and appears in no chapter of this batch as a person; she is a fact on a page, at a table in a city, making up the coast's wreck lists, with this yard's four returns in her hands.
- **The four people of the Sill** are named nowhere as persons in this batch and were asked nothing, and their limit stands and the holder did not ask twice and did not ask at all this month.

### 7. What this batch may not be used for

1. **It may not be used to name the condition.** The batch named it once, in Chapter 164, in the second column, in the holder's own left hand, with a reason, on land, and **that one naming is spent.**
2. **It may not be used to ask the bellwright, to print a digit of anything he said, or to open the chest.** He is in no chapter of it as a person and the chest was not opened.
3. **It may not be used to enter a tenth acknowledgement, to lift, narrow, re-serve or alter the notice of the thirty-first, to reopen the eight-clause plan of the seventeenth of January, to reach the plate at the fifth seam, to widen the writ's ground, to add a fifth name, to manufacture a second season, to name the man of Ashtide, to ask him anything, or to put a person, boat or lead of this yard inside the first clause of that notice on any day.**
4. **It may not be used to make a fifth return, to move the counting rule, or to report the work of the eighth and ninth of August to any office.**
5. **It may not be used to name the Nine Harbors as a compact, the Quietening, the Crown Seal, the Office of Returning Memory, Halven Rook in a room, Orison, or any of the nine final routes; to explain the nine-line mark; to identify the marking on the shard; to name the compartment; to quote a custody number's digits; to put a senior examiner in a room; to ask Sera Mott; to introduce a new antagonist, institution or final enemy; to name the man in a coat; or to put the two objects of nobody's anywhere but where they are.**
6. **It may not be used to obtain, make, release, print, quote, summarize or describe the provisional public copy record; nor to put the phrase *risk management* on a page, which is not on any page of this volume before Chapter 171; nor to produce or describe a document in which any office accepts a removal; nor to have any person in this batch state what a municipal claim does to a presumed Crown material; nor to describe a removal of a page from any file, including saying that one happened.**
7. **It may not be used to read a line of the crew's book aloud in a room, to put a seam on a document, to produce a copy of a record in a room, or to begin the volume's climax.** The book was produced whole twice and not one line of it was read out of it in either room. **THE READING OF THAT BOOK IN A ROOM IS THE VOLUME'S MIDPOINT AND IS IN CHAPTERS 181 AND LATER.**
8. **It may not be used to take a power stage, or to have a seam settle an argument, prove a motive, convict anybody, or tell Calder what happened.**
9. **It may not be used to pay Bevin Rook's forty marks, to write to him, to go to see him, to ask anybody who has seen him what he said, to reduce the figure, or to hire a boy to read a position back; to pay Mara Venn's forty marks, to pay her six marks and two days, to sign her July finding, or to reduce either; to pay the eight shillings and tenpence; to pay the bellwright; to re-write the chandler's note or move any of its three counts; to pay a shilling of the three marks owing; or to make the harbor's poverty better for anything.**
10. **It may not be used to answer the market question of the thirteenth of August, to name a compact, to resolve the coast road, to call it anything, to look at the Kettle, or to produce the reeve's chart. It may not be used to have any office answer in a room, with a seal on the table, a question this series deliberately left open.**
11. **It may not be used to fuse the lead plug with anything, to fuse the nine fastenings with the nine-line mark, to convert the nine places into the Nine Harbors, or to ask why the three places with no joint are there.**
12. **It may not be used to re-decide the refused license, to pay the thirty marks, or to argue the refusal as a decision this yard is still open on. It is a cost and not a decision, and Chapters 167 and 170 say so in the yard's own words.**
13. **It may not be used to make Mara Venn's break with the Registry happen, be foreshadowed, or be alluded to, and no chapter of the next two movements may fuse it with her leaving this crew.**

### 8. The costs this batch closes with

1. **TWO WAGES THAT WERE NOT PAID**, the week of the fifteenth of August and the week of the fifth of September, and the second of those is new in this batch, and the number of weeks fallen due with no envelope standing against them is two and not one.
2. **A REFUSAL TO CERTIFY, AND FOUR WORDS IN A FILE IN A CITY THAT THIS YARD NEVER SAID**, and no way to get at them and no letter written and no thank-you offered to a man in a city.
3. **A PRICE THAT IS NOT MONEY, AND AN ANSWER THAT IS STILL NO, AND NO MONEY CHANGING HANDS.** The ask was made, the price was named, the refusal was given, and the yard could not pay the price and did not offer it and is not going to pretend to.
4. **A MAN WHO STOOD ON STEPS FOR EIGHTY MINUTES AND THEN WENT IN**, and got nothing, and put the whole of it in the book including the going in.
5. **A DAY OF WORK REFUSED IN A DOORWAY FOR WANT OF A HOSE**, at a man's own figure, and the booking refused and no money changed hands either way, and the gland on the page since the nineteenth of May still standing unpaid and still useless.
6. **A BOY IN A JUNE BERTH, FROM A MAN OF THE THIRD LAY WHO CAME UP A HILL IN THE RAIN AND WAS NOT ASKED ONE QUESTION**, and the yard wanted to say thank you and did not say it and entered why.
7. **THE CONDITION NAMED ONCE, IN THE SECOND COLUMN, IN HIS OWN LEFT HAND, WITH A REASON, ON LAND.**
8. **THE THIRD COLUMN NOT FILLED SINCE THE FIRST OF AUGUST**, and the shipwright's first-column entry saying she could have filled it and did not and why.
9. **A MOORING THAT IS IN SERVICE AND IS HARBOR GROUND AND IS NOT THIS YARD'S**, and a favor that belongs to a man of the third lay, and a man sent to a tide gang four men short, and a day and a half of that gang as the whole of the price.
10. **A FIGURE IN TYPE IN A CITY BESIDE A FIGURE IN TYPE IN A CITY, AND NEITHER ABLE TO CHECK THE OTHER, AND A PENNY SPENT ON A STALL TO FIND OUT.**
11. **THE REFUSED LICENSE, TAKEN OUT OF THE WRIT AND PUT BACK, AND THE THIRTY MARKS' ARITHMETIC SAID OUT LOUD ONCE IN FOUR VOLUMES AND NOT TWICE.**
12. **A FIGURE READ OUT AT THE HEAD OF A DOCK IN FORTY PEOPLE'S HEARING, OFF THE YARD'S OWN BOOK, TWICE, AND IT DID NOTHING.**
13. **A HARBOR POORER ON THE THIRTIETH OF SEPTEMBER THAN IT WAS ON THE ELEVENTH, AND THE CISTERN WALKED ON NONE OF ITS EIGHT CHARGES.**

**None applied to any file outside the four state files. Eight author-level decisions taken on the page, and one prompt figure corrected by the chapters.**

### 6. The Tranter and Rorke paper chain, which had three steps that could not all be true

**THE THREE DOCUMENTS ARE NOW ONE SEQUENCE WITH DATES THAT CLOSE, AND THE REVIEWER'S OWN SUGGESTION — *give the three documents one sequence with dates that close, or separate them explicitly on the page* — IS WHAT WAS DONE.**

1. **The document Tranter described on Friday the twenty-second and carried up the hill on Monday the twenty-fifth IS the surveyor's report, and the vessel in it IS HIS OWN.** `chapter-0166.md:7` gave him a coaster of about two hundred tons where the report and his own account both give a hundred and ninety tons; **it now says about a hundred and ninety tons.** He said on the Friday that the paper was *not about a wreck*, which is not a thing a man says about a report on the total loss of his own coaster; **it now says *it is not a salvage paper*.**
2. **THE SURVEYOR NEVER ASKED THE YARD FOR AN ANSWER AND GOT ONE. SHE ASKED IN WRITING, GOT NO ANSWER, AND RECORDED WHAT SHE HAD HEARD AS HER OWN FINDING, WITH THE SOURCE ON THE FACE OF THE ENTRY.** `chapter-0168.md:23` read *I have applied to the yard … and I am informed that the yard declines to certify the figure*, which put a refusal in a document dated before the refusal was made and left the yard's first column claiming it did not know. **It now reads that she has applied in writing, has had no answer, records the yard as declining to certify the figure, and records on the face of that entry that she has not had it from the yard and has it from a man of the first lay who crossed the water to tell her so, and that she would rather set it down with that on it than leave it off — which is a working person's own hedge and is the volume's turn arriving through a trade's habit rather than through a plot.**
3. **TRANTER'S *SATURDAY* IS GONE BECAUSE NO REFUSAL HAD BEEN MADE, AND HIS *FRIDAY* WITH IT.** The only Saturday before Monday the twenty-fifth is the nineteenth, and the yard says no on the Monday, so a Saturday letter could only have reported a refusal that had not been made. A Friday letter has the same defect, because the report that quotes it came on the Saturday boat of the nineteenth. `chapter-0168.md:25` now reads that he told the surveyor **in a letter in the first week of September, before he came up the hill on the Friday, that a yard which has printed a figure of its own cannot be got to swear to it afterwards; that the surveyor had that in her hand when she wrote the line; and that he has not sent this party one word of that letter and is not going to, and has not asked the yard yet, and is going to now.** **THE WHOLE CHAIN NOW CLOSES AND THE ORDER IS THE POINT: a letter early in the first week of September, the report written on the back of that letter and sent so that it came on the Saturday boat of the nineteenth, described in this yard on Friday the twenty-second, read out of a coat pocket on Monday the twenty-fifth, the yard's own refusal given in a doorway at about half past ten on the twenty-fifth — the first refusal anybody made, and it was already in a file in a city — the answer written on Tuesday the twenty-sixth and up the hill with the morning boat on the twenty-seventh.** Nothing is reported that has not happened, and nothing happens before the thing that reports it.
4. **THE REPLY HAS A DATE THAT FITS.** `chapter-0169.md:11` had the surveyor writing back *on Friday*, and no Friday falls between Tranter's letter of Monday night the twenty-fifth and the morning of Wednesday the twenty-seventh. **It now says he wrote back on Tuesday night and it came up on the Wednesday with the morning boat**, which closes against the letter's own opening line, *I have your letter of the twenty-fifth*.
5. **THE YARD'S FIRST COLUMN NOW RECORDS WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED TO IT.** `chapter-0168.md:69` said the report recorded that the surveyor *applied to this party … and that this party declines to certify it*, and then that this party does not know who sent the paper. **It now records that a letter from that city came into this yard in the ordinary post, is in that letter box, was not answered on the day it came and has not been answered since; that the yard gave that answer in a doorway at about half past ten on the instant and is not going to put it in a letter either, and why — that a man who asks a yard to stand behind a number in a city is asking for a name under it, and the answer to a question like that is given to a man in his own mouth and not on paper; and that the *who sent it* clause is about the paper in the coat pocket.** The two are no longer in conflict and the letter is a new fact on the page rather than a hole in one.

**THE TURN IS PAID IN THE VOLUME'S OWN TERMS, TWICE, IN ITS OWN FORMS. On Friday the ninth of October, at about half past ten in the morning, at a copying counter in a room off the fish market, a woman of thirty was handed a card of about four inches by three in the hand of the circuit office of this harbor, and on the card, in the Registry's own column, against the reason, are the two words *risk management*. On Thursday the fifteenth, a paper served on this party in a doorway says, in a document, that a leaf of the Registry's file of the ASTER GANNET is called for and is not produced, and that the reason of the non-production is on a form of the Registry's own dated the second of September which is not to be produced to the party. THE PHRASE IS ON THREE PAGES OF THIS BATCH AND IT IS NOT THREE DISCOVERIES: it is one form filled in twice and a party reading it out once in a shed, and that is the horror and not a mystery. The sentence the whole of it pays — *a document is a thing an office says about itself* — is said out loud by a person of no office at a copying counter in Chapter 175 and again in a doorway in Chapter 176 and again by the holder in the shed in Chapter 180, and each of the three is in that woman's or that man's own mouth.**

### 1. The calendar the batch actually ran on

**WHAT THE TEN CHAPTERS RUN ON IS SET FROM THE CHAPTERS AND FROM NOTHING ELSE, AND IT IS NOT THE GRID `outline/volume-04.md` PRINTED IN LOCK L1. THE SENTENCE THAT STOOD HERE — *The book's grid, per lock L1, and no weekday was corrected to an almanac* — WAS WRONG FOR THIS BATCH AND IS WITHDRAWN AND NAMED AS WITHDRAWN RATHER THAN SILENTLY REPLACED; this review certified the batch's weekdays against each other and not against the lock, and lock L1 is amended at its foot at the Batch 0004 review, where the whole of the change, the place it falls and the three reasons it is not repaired in the text are set out. The ten chapters state, and the day list is right because the chapters say it:** 1 October a **Thursday** and a rota day · 2 **Friday** · 3 **Saturday** · 4 **Sunday** · 5 **Monday** · 6 **Tuesday** and a wage week · 7 **Wednesday** · 8 **Thursday** and a rota day · 9 **Friday** · 10 **Saturday** · 11 **Sunday** · 12 **Monday** · 13 **Tuesday** and a wage week · 14 **Wednesday** · 15 **Thursday** and a rota day · 16 **Friday** · 17 **Saturday** · 18 **Sunday** · 19 **Monday** · 20 **Tuesday** and a wage week. The distribution is the prompt's own and was followed without a shift.

**THE CHAPTERS SET THE WEEKDAY AND THE FILE FOLLOWS THEM, WHICH IS LOCK L1'S OWN RULE.** October is a Thursday the first, and every weekday the batch states is a weekday that follows from it. **THE FIFTEENTH OF OCTOBER IS A THURSDAY AND IS A ROTA DAY, AND CHAPTER 178'S INVENTORY CHARGES THE CISTERN ON THE FIRST, THE FIFTH, THE EIGHTH, THE TWELFTH AND THE FIFTEENTH — FIVE CHARGES IN THE MONTH UP TO THAT FRIDAY, AND THE FIFTEENTH IS THE EIGHTEENTH SINCE THE THIRD OF AUGUST.** **NO WEEKDAY IS NOW STATED FOR ANY DAY IN SEPTEMBER OR BEFORE, AND THAT IS A REPAIR AND NOT A LOSS: the counterfoil of the second, the paper served on the party and the first-column entries all say *the second day of September* or *the second*, and Chapter 180's account of the month said *Friday the second of September* in one line, which no document in the batch supports. The counterfoil's date is the second and the job sheet's date is the eighth and the copying was done on the eighth, six days after the slip was filled, and the form itself now says so on its face.**

**THE HEARING ROOM'S SLATE WALL CAME DOWN BARE THREE TIMES IN THIS BATCH AND NO SITTING WAS HELD ON ANY OF THEM:** Monday the fifth of October (**twenty-second** Mondays since the first of May, Ch 173), Monday the twelfth (**twenty-third**, Ch 176), and Monday the nineteenth (**twenty-fourth**, Ch 180). The first of October is a Thursday and is not a Monday and is not counted. **THE COUNTER DID NOT RESTART.** The last of September was **twenty-one** and is Batch 0002's.

**THE HEARING ROOM AND THE MARKET WALL ARE NEVER THE SAME DAY, AND IT IS VERIFIED A FOURTH TIME.** **THE MARKET WALL WAS NOT TOUCHED ON ANY DAY OF THIS BATCH** — no sheet went up and no sheet came off, and the sheets of the fifteenth and the twenty-fifth of August are still on the nails, the yard's own fourth return of the fourteenth of July still under the twenty-fifth. The hearing room is used **once**, on **Friday the sixteenth of October**, for a sitting of about forty minutes. The market office is used **once**, on **Tuesday the thirteenth of October**. No two of the three rooms share a day. **The market office is NOT the market wall and the two are not treated as the same room anywhere in the batch.**

### 2. The money chain, mark by mark, and where it closes

A mark is a hundred and sixty pence and a shilling is twelve, so the whole of the arithmetic in this batch hangs on those two figures and both of them are checkable in the prose.** **The batch closes four pence lighter than it opened, and the four pence is the postage of one letter in the ordinary post, and that is the whole of what this yard spent on itself in twenty days.**

### 3. FOUR FIGURES THE CHAPTERS DECIDED, AND THE PROMPT FIGURES THEY CORRECT

1. **THE WAGE OF TUESDAY THE SIXTH OF OCTOBER WAS NOT PAID, AND THE NUMBER OF WEEKS FALLEN DUE WITH NO ENVELOPE IS THREE AND NOT TWO.** The prompt's hard rule 2 states *two weeks fallen due this year have no envelope standing against them, being the week of Tuesday the fifteenth of August and the week of Tuesday the fifth of September.* **Chapter 173 adds the sixth of October, entered unpaid on the Tuesday with the figure and the date and the reason, and carries the figure at three in the first column of Chapters 173, 174, 176, 177, 178 and 180, and the two older weeks in the same breath every time.**
2. **THE POSTAGE OF THE LETTER OF THE SECOND OF OCTOBER IS FOUR PENCE, AND IT IS THE ONLY MONEY THIS YARD HAS SPENT ON ITSELF IN TWENTY DAYS, AND IT IS NOT THE SEVEN PENCE.** Nessa Pike's seven pence for the postage of the letter of the twentieth of August stands unpaid, out of her own pocket, and the shipwright said in the shed on the second of October, in front of two people, that if the two figures are ever put on one line in that book she will take the book off the bench. The two figures are carried in the first column of Chapters 171, 173, 177, 178, 179 and 180 and never once together.
3. **THE TWO OBJECTS OF NOBODY'S: about a hundred and thirty-seven days on the first of October and about a hundred and forty-nine days on the twentieth, about nine feet apart, under two tarpaulins, one of them with a corner off it since the seventeenth of June and not lashed back, AND NEITHER OBJECT HAS MOVED.** Counted once in each chapter in which it is mentioned and never twice in the same chapter.
4. **A MAN OF THE FIRST LAY OF ABOUT NINETY TONS ASKED ABOUT A THING ON HIS STEM ON THE SEVENTEENTH OF OCTOBER AND WAS TOLD NO** — the same unnamed man who asked about the mooring at the ninth seam in Chapter 165 — **and he said he had not expected it in October and would come again in the spring.** He is not asked anything further and nothing is taken.

### 4. Every document and instrument created, quoted, or discovered in this batch

1. **A COPYING JOB SHEET**, the head of it in the hand of a woman of a copyist's trade: *Job 4 — Fri. 8 Sept — Morrow circuit office, copying room. From the file of the ASTER GANNET. Leaf 62. One leaf, copied entire, eleven sheets, returned with the file.* **The yard read those four lines twice and did not read the rest of it and did not ask to**, and the woman said in that yard that the remainder came out of that office's file and were not hers and that she did not look at them. **THE NUMBER ENTERED IN THE FIRST COLUMN IS SIXTY-TWO, AND IT IS A LEAF OF A FILE AND NOT A NUMBER ON ANY OBJECT, AND NO NUMBER ON ANY OBJECT IS IN THIS HARBOR'S HANDS.** **THE ELEVEN SHEETS AND THE BOARD ARE THE SAME ELEVEN SHEETS: she carried the whole of the job up the hill on a flat board, being the eleven she had copied and her own sheet of them and the office's slip, and Chapter 171 now says thirteen and names all three.**
2. **A letter in the ordinary post, the second of October**, four lines in the holder's own left hand, to a man of the first lay who has a boat of about **a hundred and ninety tons** and who wanted the figure of the bar of gravel so that he could put his word under a line in a paper of his own. Four pence, paid at a counter in the holder's own hand. **It is a refusal, in writing, of a thing already refused in a doorway, and it is entered as a decision and not as a virtue.**
3. **A WITHDRAWAL COUNTERFOIL**, the volume's central document, handed over at a copying counter on the ninth of October and read in a doorway on the twelfth: *Morrow circuit office — copying room. Second day of September. Withdrawn: file of the ASTER GANNET, leaf 62. One leaf, to the copying room on the eighth instant, copied entire, returned with the file. On the application of a commissioned officer of the Crown Navy, by letter of the first instant, a copy of which letter is on the file. This office agrees to the withdrawal. **Reason entered by this office: risk management.** The leaf is not to be produced. A copy is held.* **IT IS IN THE REGISTRY'S OWN HAND AGAINST ITS OWN REASON, AND IT IS A THING AN OFFICE SAYS ABOUT ITSELF, AND IT IS DATED THE SECOND OF SEPTEMBER, WHICH IS BEFORE THE CREW'S BOOK WENT INTO A FILE ON THE NINTH AND BEFORE THE NOTICE OF THE TENTH. THE FORM AND THE JOB SHEET ARE TWO DOCUMENTS WITH TWO DATES AND ONE WITHDRAWAL, AND THEY ARE NO LONGER WORD-FOR-WORD THE SAME LINE: the slip is filled on the day the leaf comes out, its top copy goes into the removal register at the end of that day's work, the counterfoil comes to the woman who did the copying, and the copying was done on the eighth, six days later, and the form says the eighth on its own face. THE PARTY THAT WAS PAID ON THE TWENTIETH, WHICH IS NINETEEN DAYS AFTER THE FIRST, IS PAID.**
4. **THE FOOT OF A COPYIST'S JOB SHEET**, in that woman's own hand and not the office's: that the copy of leaf 62 is to be read with leaf 88. **LEAF 88 IS THE ONLY THING IN THE BATCH THAT NOBODY HAS SEEN AND EVERYONE CAN CHECK, AND ITS EXISTENCE IS CHECKED BY TWO PEOPLE IN THIS TOWN AND ITS CONTENTS BY NOBODY.**
5. **A fair copy of four sheets of a conservator's own writing**, at a penny a sheet in a room off the fish market, charged and paid, with a leaf number at the head of it written by the woman herself: **leaf 62, the leaf of her own refusal of the eleventh of November last, on four grounds, in her own hand, with her trade against her name, a date, and the office's stamp on it because she would not let it leave without one.** The first of those four grounds is that the office will not countersign an instrument that puts a person inside a closure that the same office's own notice created.
6. **A letter of four lines from that woman to that office**, written on Sunday the eleventh and put in the post at about half past two, at a penny out of her own pocket: that she will not be cited, quoted, produced, or asked again by that office or by any office of it; that no form, sheet, notation, hand or date of hers is to be used to support an account she did not write and has not read; and that she is not resigning anything, **because there is nothing to resign from, and that is the reason she is writing it on paper instead of saying it in a room, and she has been waiting eleven months to find out what to call the thing and it turns out that it has a name and the name is a form.** **HER BREAK WITH THE REGISTRY IS THIS AND IT IS A DIFFERENT EVENT FROM HER LEAVING THIS CREW AND IT IS NOT FUSED WITH IT ANYWHERE IN THE TEN CHAPTERS.**
7. **A letter of Wil Tranter to Ailsa Rorke**, read out in a doorway on the sixth of October and given to the yard: that he will not set his word under her finding, and his reason in full, and that a man's name under a line about water is the only thing a man of the first lay has that a man of no lay does not have. **The yard cannot use it and entered that it cannot, and offered him nothing, and he would not have it.**
8. **A paper of six paragraphs served on this party in a doorway at about eleven in the morning on Thursday the fifteenth of October**, by Ambrose Sell, clerk of the circuit office and clerk of that sitting, who gave his name and the name of his office before he read it. It appoints **Friday the sixteenth of October instant at ten of the morning at the hearing room over the tide-gang store on the west basin**; it requires the four parties to attend; it requires the six things of the fourth paragraph of the notice of the tenth again and says that the production of them is not a concession and is not an admission; it says a schedule of records is read into the record and that a copy is not given to any party; **it states that the registry file of the ASTER GANNET is before the inquiry, that one leaf is called for and is not produced, and that the reason of the non-production is entered by the Registry on a form of its own dated the second of September, a copy of which is on the record, and that the form is not before the sitting and is not to be produced to the party**; and it says nothing touches the second season. Signed **A. Sell, clerk.**
9. **THE MAGISTRATE'S NAME, ON PAPER ONLY.** The magistrate of the circuit is *Halven Rook* and the name stands at the foot of the ORIGINAL of the paper, in a file in a city, and is not on the copy, and the clerk said so out loud in a doorway: *it is on a paper and not in a room.* **He has not been in this harbor, is not going to be, and appears in no chapter of this batch as a person and in no room.**
10. **A SCHEDULE OF RECORDS READ INTO THE RECORD IN ABOUT FOUR MINUTES.** A list and a list is read out. The file of the ASTER GANNET is fourth on it. Leaf 62 called for. Leaf 62 not produced. The reason is on a form of the Registry's own of the second of September. The form was not produced. **THE TWO WORDS ARE NOT IN THE SCHEDULE AND WERE NOT READ OUT IN THAT ROOM, AND THE YARD HAS THE TWO WORDS FROM A WOMAN AT A COUNTER AND NOT FROM ANY OFFICE.**
11. **A RECORD IN A CITY, MADE ON THE SIXTEENTH OF OCTOBER, OF ELEVEN SENTENCES IN THE HOLDER'S OWN WORDS, read back to him and entered:** that there is a person in this harbor whose hand is on a page of that file and who is not an officer of any office in it; that she is not on this crew and is not of this yard and is not a holder and is not on the four names of the writ; **and that he is not going to give her name and is not going to say that she is in this harbor.** He entered against himself, on the eighteenth of September, in the first column, in his own left hand and in advance, that this party is not going to put a name on a thing it cannot check, and the entry stands and the cost of it is on the page with the date and the hour against it.
