- **The writ.** Granted Monday the first of May, running to midnight on the first of March next, not the Second Bell license, not a charter, renewing nothing, ground not widened, four names and no fifth. **THE SECOND SEASON IS A NAMED ABSENCE AND NOTHING IN THIS BATCH TOUCHES IT, GRANTS IT, REFUSES IT OR DEALS WITH IT, AND CHAPTER 172 ENTERS THAT THIS PARTY CONSIDERED GOING TO THE HARBOR AUTHORITY FOR ONE THING AND DID NOT.**
- **The notice of the thirty-first of October.** Not lifted, not narrowed, not re-served, not altered. **NO PERSON, NO BOAT AND NO LEAD OF THIS YARD WAS INSIDE THE FIRST CLAUSE ON ANY DAY OF THIS BATCH, and this is not entered this month because nothing happened.** The two objects of nobody's: about a hundred and forty-nine days and neither has moved.
- **The acknowledgements: eight, the ninth entered on the twenty-eighth of August by this party, the tenth may not be entered. THIS BATCH ENTERED NONE, ASKED FOR NONE, AND ENTERED IN CHAPTER 172 THAT IT CONSIDERED ONE THING AND DID NOT ASK, AND WHY.**
- **The plate at the fifth seam is in eleven feet, seen and not measured and not touched. THE NOTE STANDS OPEN. THE EIGHT-CLAUSE PLAN OF THE SEVENTEENTH OF JANUARY IS REFUSED IN A RECORD WITH A DATE ON IT AND THIS PARTY HAS NOT WRITTEN A LETTER ABOUT THE PLATE SINCE THE TWENTY-NINTH OF MARCH. THE MECHANISM IS NAMED AS AN OFFICE'S PAPER TWICE IN THIS BATCH — in the first column of Chapter 171 and in the first column of Chapter 174 — and on the eighth of October the party entered against itself that it does not know whether the removal of a leaf from a file in a second-floor room is the same thing as the change of politics in an office it has been waiting for since the seventeenth of January, and that it is not going to guess, and that a number in a book is not a change of politics in an office. THE NOTE IS NOT CLOSED IN THIS BATCH AND IS NOT REQUIRED TO BE.**
- **The bell is off the south end in eight and a half feet and is not going out and is not going to go out inside four years. NO BOAT WENT OFF THE SOUTH END IN THIS BATCH, NO SECOND EIGHT MARKS WAS ENTERED AS PAID, THE PHRASE *a tongue half worn through* DOES NOT OCCUR, THE BELLWRIGHT WAS NOT ASKED AND IS IN NO CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH AS A PERSON, AND THE CHEST WAS NOT OPENED AND WAS NOT BROUGHT DOWN THE HILL.**
- **The lead plug. Not asked about, not printed, not opened, and not brought down the hill.** The undertaking of the second of July binds the yard and not the office and not the market and not the boy.
- **THE CONDITION IS NAMED NOWHERE IN THIS BATCH.** The bare fact is carried twice with a reason against each line and without a name, in the second column of Chapter 172 and in the second column of Chapter 179. **The four lines above the named line of the twentieth of July are still four, are still nameless, and are not struck out, and a request to strike one out is refused in the same words it is refused for a line in any column, and the count of four stands in the first column in a ship's hand with no name against it.**
- **The glass storm.** Not used, not referred to, and no cause named for it in this batch or in any volume.
- **The coast road.** Not resolved, not called anything by anybody, and neither figure for the bar of gravel is withdrawn. **THE KETTLE WAS NOT LOOKED AT AND FIVE MILES OF THAT COAST HAS NOT BEEN LOOKED AT. THE REFUSED LICENSE IS NOT RE-DECIDED AND IS NOT MENTIONED OUTSIDE THE STANDING INVENTORY.**
- **The run under this town.** Not explained, not named, not pursued, and not referred to.
- **Custody.** Three items, three numbers, no digit quoted, none returns, none is asked for, the municipal claim on the third stands, and the word does not occur once in the ten chapters of this batch. **THE LIVE QUESTION — what a municipal claim does to a presumed Crown material — IS NOT ANSWERED AND IS NOT PUT TO ANYBODY.**
- **The concealment.** Hidden. The Oren mark is in no record, in no office, in no book and not in the reeve's chart notation.
- **The delayed note.** Eleven logged occasions and two of them with no call in them. **NEITHER COUNT WAS ADVANCED IN THIS BATCH BY ARITHMETIC OR BY A MEASUREMENT. NO OCCASION WAS ENTERED AND NO MEASUREMENT WAS TAKEN AND THE DELAY IS A HAND'S WIDTH OF A SECOND AND HAS NOT MOVED AND NOBODY IN THIS HARBOR HAS EVER SAID WHY AND THIS PARTY IS NOT GOING TO BE THE FIRST.**
- **Labor.** No air bought in this batch and no hose and no gland paid and no day of work done that wanted one. **Two days of work at the second seam's own face, at five marks and at three marks, and a day of about three marks on a wharf refused for want of a crew of two and a half in the week before a sitting, and a day that was there to be booked and was not booked for a reason of this harbor's and not of this yard's.** Two wages paid and one not. One herring berth out. The north berth out. The tide gang four men short. **THE CISTERN ON A ROTA OF A MONDAY AND A THURSDAY, CHARGED AT NO FIGURE ON THE FIRST, FIFTH, EIGHTH, TWELFTH, FIFTEENTH AND NINETEENTH OF OCTOBER, WHICH IS SIX DAYS, AND ON THIRTEEN DAYS BEFORE THAT, AND THIS PARTY WALKED NONE OF THE NINETEEN AND HAS NOT WALKED ONE SINCE THE THIRD OF AUGUST.** **THE FIFTEENTH IS STAGED, NOT INVENTED: it is in Chapter 178's inventory of Thursday the fifteenth and again in Chapter 179's, and Chapter 179 adds in prose that the Thursday the fifteenth was the eighteenth charge since the third of August. The run is fourteen on the first, fifteen on the fifth, sixteen on the eighth, seventeen on the twelfth, eighteen on the fifteenth and nineteen on the nineteenth, and that sequence is now in the chapters and can be read off them. THE FIFTEENTH IS THE ONE CHARGE OF THE MONTH THAT THIS PARTY KNOWS OF AT SECOND HAND: a man of the third lay told it at the head of the dock on the seventeenth that the cistern had been charged on the Thursday morning and not on the Monday, and the party entered that it did not know that and entered that it does not know it now, and it counted the charge in the run anyway, which is what a run of charges is.** The mole-head light not on. The fire party's hose dead until the spring. The hard at Ashtide unanswered since the ninth of November. Nineteen winters in a naval file and in a list being made up in a city, and nobody in Morrow Quay will ever be able to check what she writes with them. The *Sea Wren* at the pile and this party has not thanked him and has not been asked to. Neave Tarrant, nine winters, out since the twenty-eighth of February, not found, one line, and this party has not gone.
- **THE READ-OUT DEVICE WAS NOT USED IN THIS BATCH AND ITS USE IS CARRIED FORWARD.** The read-out — a man reading figures out of the yard's own book aloud to people who can check them — is the batch's one-use-per-batch device and **Chapter 171 enters in the first column that the fourth time this yard published something had cost four pence and that the party does not know what the fifth will cost and is not going to find out by not spending it, and no read-out was made in this batch.** The read-back — the ship's hand reading the day's entries back and the holder reading them back after her, nobody else in the shed — runs in **FOUR of the ten chapters, 172, 178, 179 and 180**, and is not a use of the device and may be used on any night without spending anything. **THE FIGURE OF SEVEN THAT THIS FILE CARRIED BEFORE THESE REPAIRS IS WITHDRAWN AND NAMED AS WITHDRAWN HERE: 173, 175, 176 and 177 have no read-back on any page, and 178 has one at its seventy-first line and was the chapter the earlier count left out. The method is a plain one and can be re-run: a chapter carries a read-back if the words *read back* or *read-back* appear in it, and a search of the ten chapters returns 172, 178, 179 and 180 and nothing else.**

### 6. The people, and the four who are not in a room

- **Calder Marr**, thirty-two. **HE GOES IN NO WATER IN THIS BATCH AND NO POT OF AIR IS BOUGHT.** He is in a doorway, a shed, a market office, a hearing room once, and a copying counter he does not go to. **He reads no seam, on a document or on anything else, and the word *faultreader* is on no page of the ten chapters and no seam settles anything, proves anything, convicts anybody or tells him what happened.** He refused to be a door, wrote a refusal into a letterbox, found out he could not remember one line of his own second column, entered a decision to tell Mara Venn a thing and did not tell her and gave the reason twice, put a true sentence about a person into a record in a city on the sixteenth, and counted five things he could do in a shed on the twentieth and four of them cost money he has not got.
- **Nessa Pike**, twenty-seven. The tender, the pump, the fall, the board and the slate, and the standing shutdown. **She had nine sentences in her head on the seventeenth of October and did not write them down and said why out loud and asked for it to be in the book in her own hand and not his.** She read the two-column figures at the head of a dock on the thirteenth in about two minutes and did not answer the one man who said the thing out loud. She said *a wall has nothing in it you can be made to answer for and a room has a person in it and a clerk with a pen*, and the party entered that it is not going to improve on it in a market. **She has not been thanked and is not going to ask.**
- **Mara Venn**, thirty. **NOT ON THE CREW, NOT ASKED FOR ANYTHING BY THIS PARTY, AND SHE CAME UP THE HILL ON THE TWELFTH UNASKED AND UNSENT AND ASKED FOR NOTHING.** She found out at a copying counter on the ninth, in a room open to anybody, from a woman of fifty-eight who is a mentor of hers. **She priced nothing and asked for nothing and was paid nothing and gave nothing, and refused to give the line, and gave the reason: that the price she named in the market office on the twenty-ninth of September has not changed because a file has come to us, and that a line of hers in a book of the yard would be a document and the Registry's page is a document, and that two documents in one room and only one of them carrying a seal is how a person of no office becomes a thing a person with an office can use.** **She left the Registry in her own words, in a letter in the ordinary post, before anybody asked her, and it is not a crew and it is not a yard and it is not a resignation because there is nothing to resign from. SHE DID NOT COME BACK TO THIS CREW AND IS NOT ON IT. HER FORTY MARKS STAND UNPAID, FIRST AFTER FOOD, SINCE THE FIFTEENTH OF OCTOBER, AND THE SIX MARKS AND TWO DAYS WERE NOT OFFERED, PAID OR REDUCED. SHE IS NOT COMING TO THE MARKET OFFICE OF THIS TOWN ON A TUESDAY OR A FRIDAY MORNING ANY MORE, AND THE REASON IS HER OWN AND IS NOT GOING TO BE GIVEN, AND THE YARD DID NOT ARRANGE IT AND IS NOT GOING TO UN-ARRANGE IT.**
- **Ors Kest**, forty-four. **HE IS IN NO CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH AS A PERSON AND WAS NOT ASKED FOR ANYTHING.** The yard entered in the first column on the fourth of October that it considered going to that office for a record of the harbor's own ground for the week of the eighth of August and did not go, and gave the reason: the ninth is the last entry in that ledger, a tenth may not be entered, the price of the ninth fell on a man of the first lay out of a Monday and has not been paid, and a yard that has been told in the open air that its ledger is spent does not go back up the same steps with the same request. **Entered as a decision and not as a virtue, and nobody is going to thank this party for it.**
- **Ambrose Sell**, clerk of the circuit office and clerk of the sitting. **NAMED WHEREVER A CLERK OF THE CIRCUIT OFFICE APPEARS, in Chapter 178 only.** He served the paper in a doorway, named the magistrate, said he has read what the Registry's form says and will not say it and will not say that he has read it, and asked one question in a room and entered the answer. **He is the mouth of a clause and not an antagonist and he has not become one.**
- **Pernel Saye**, fifty-eight, of this harbor, a copyist, with a counter in a room off the fish market that is open to anybody from eight until the market is off the boards, where a sheet is a penny and forty sheets a shilling. **NEW IN THIS BATCH, NAMED, ORDINARY, IN HER OWN TRADE'S WORDS, AND NOT A VILLAIN AND NOT ON ANY LADDER AND NOT GIVEN A TITLE, A UNIFORM, A COMMISSION OR A MOTIVE THAT IS NOT A COPYIST'S.** She has been up the stairs to that room twice in her life and is not going a third time. She keeps nine years of counterfoils in a box under her counter and has never thrown one away. She copied eleven sheets on the eighth of September and was paid at the going rate on the twentieth and did not go and ask. **She taught a woman of thirty to write a leaf number at the head of a sheet, and that is the whole of what she taught her and it is the whole of what was needed.** She came up the hill on the first of October, unasked and at her own cost, and was not thanked and did not ask to be.
- **Oswin Rede**, about fifty, of the first lay, a boat of his own, a boy of nineteen on the second lay with four weeks this year. **NEW IN THIS BATCH, NAMED, ORDINARY, AND SENT DOWN A HILL ONCE BY THIS PARTY.** He asked a room in the market office on the thirteenth for the sense of a form with a tide conservator's hand on it, and the room could not give it, and he came up this hill on the Wednesday and asked this party, and was told the truth in about nine sentences, and said he is not owed anything by this yard and that nobody in this yard has asked him for a thing. **HE SAYS HE CAME UP THE HILL TWICE AND THAT HE ASKED A MAN IN A DOORWAY ON THE SATURDAY AS WELL, AND THAT IS HIS OWN CLAIM AND IT IS NOT ON A PAGE OF THIS BATCH; THE YARD SAW HIM ONCE AND HAS ENTERED THAT IT DOES NOT KNOW THE REST OF IT AND IS NOT GOING TO ASK.**
- **Wil Tranter**, of the first lay, fifty-one, master of a coaster of about a hundred and ninety tons. **He refused a surveyor in a city to put his word under a line about water, gave the reason in his own hand, brought the letter up the hill unasked, and would not take a shilling for it and said out loud that he would rather it was on the page that the yard offered and he would not have it. HE IS NOT THANKED AND DOES NOT ASK TO BE.**
- **The press-keeper at the market office**, a woman who has worked in that room for nineteen years and whose mother shifted the slab. She has set about nine hundred sheets since the fifteenth of August at a shilling the forty and has never been asked what is on one and has not read one. **She has been asked three times this month by men with money to bring the slab forward and has not, and told the yard so because the yard had not asked her for anything and it cost her nothing to say it out loud.**
- **A man of the first lay of about ninety tons**, unnamed, who asked about the mooring at the ninth seam in Chapter 165 and about a thing on his stem in Chapter 179 and was told no both times and is coming back in the spring.
- **A woman of the third lay**, unnamed, who could not book a day on the seventh of October because the third lay is short and the tide gang is four men short and one herring berth of two is out and her vessel has a started plank, and who told this party so instead of not coming.
- **A man of the third lay**, unnamed, who offered a wharf day for Monday the twelfth and was refused and said he had had a Monday out of a month this year as well, and who is to come back on it after the seventeenth.
- **Alden Marr**, sixty-one. **AT THE FAR BENCH ON SIX DAYS OF THIS BATCH — the second, the fifth, the eighth, the twelfth, the eighteenth and the nineteenth of October — and on no other day in it**, not asked for anything on any of the six and asking nothing on any of the six, and Calder Marr did not go over to him on any of the six. **THE FIGURE OF SEVEN AND THE DAYS OF THE FIRST AND THE SIXTEENTH ARE WITHDRAWN AND NAMED AS WITHDRAWN: the chapters place him at the far bench on the second (Ch171), the fifth (Ch173), the eighth (Ch174), the twelfth (Ch176), the eighteenth (Ch179) and the nineteenth (Ch180), and on no other day of the batch. Chapter 180's first-column entry listed the first and the sixteenth, which no chapter stages, and left the second out, and that entry now carries six days and the six days the prose supports. THIS IS THE SECOND TIME THE BATCH-0002 REVIEW HAS HAD TO CORRECT A FAR-BENCH FIGURE AGAINST THE CHAPTERS, AND THE RULE IT LEFT BEHIND IS THE RULE THAT FIXED IT: A FIRST-COLUMN ENTRY AND THE PROSE HAVE TO AGREE WITH EACH OTHER ABOUT HOW MANY DAYS A MAN SAT ON A BENCH, AND NEITHER MAY BE CORRECTED TOWARD THE OTHER WITHOUT READING THE CHAPTER.** **ON THE SUNDAY THE EIGHTEENTH AT ABOUT ELEVEN IN THE MORNING THE HOLDER PUT A TIN CUP OF WATER ON THE END OF THAT BENCH AND WENT BACK TO HIS OWN BENCH AND SAID NOTHING, AND THE MAN DID NOT TURN ROUND AND DID NOT DRINK IT AND DID NOT REFUSE IT AND SAID NO WORD, AND THE CUP WAS STILL THERE ON THE MONDAY MORNING AT NINE AND WAS NOT THERE AT FOUR IN THE AFTERNOON, AND NEITHER BROTHER SAW WHO TOOK IT AND NEITHER BROTHER HAS SAID A WORD ABOUT IT AND NEITHER BROTHER IS GOING TO.** The holder entered on the Sunday that he has done that once and is not going to do it again, and why: that a cup of water on the end of a bench is a question in a language this party made up, and this party does not get to make up a language for a man who has not been asked anything. **No fragment, no report talk, no second story, no confession, and he is not named in any chapter of this batch except as the man on the bench.**
- **Bevin Rook is in no chapter of this batch as a person.** The three nots stand. The head of the third column keeps his hand. Forty marks stand whole. **The third column has not been filled since the first of August and was not filled on any day of this batch and nobody has been appointed to it.**
- **Captain Veyra Holt** does not come to this harbor, is not in a room, and appears in no chapter of this batch as a person; she is a fact on a page, at a table in a city, making up the coast's wreck lists, with this yard's four returns in her hands.
- **The four people of the Sill** are named nowhere as persons in this batch, were asked nothing, and their limit stands and the holder did not ask twice and did not ask at all this month.
- **The man in a coat of an office in a city IS NOT NAMED IN THIS BATCH AND MAY NOT BE NAMED IN THIS VOLUME.** He is in no chapter of it and in no room in it. He is a channel and not a face. **The commissioned officer of the Crown Navy who applied by letter for leaf 62 on the first of September is not named, is not described, and is not guessed at, and the yard entered that it does not know and has not asked and is not going to guess.**

### 7. What this batch may not be used for

1. **It may not be used to name the condition.** The batch named it nowhere. The bare fact is carried twice, in the second column, with a reason, and without a name.
2. **It may not be used to ask the bellwright, to print a digit of anything he said on the second of July, or to open the chest.** He is in no chapter of it as a person and the chest was not opened.
3. **It may not be used to enter a tenth acknowledgement, to lift, narrow, re-serve or alter the notice of the thirty-first, to reopen the eight-clause plan of the seventeenth of January, to reach the plate at the fifth seam, to close the plate note, to widen the writ's ground, to add a fifth name, to manufacture a second season, to name the man of Ashtide, to ask him anything, or to put a person, boat or lead of this yard inside the first clause of that notice on any day.**
4. **It may not be used to make a fifth return, to move the counting rule, or to report the work of the eighth and ninth of August to any office.**
5. **It may not be used to name the Nine Harbors as a compact, the Quietening, the Crown Seal, the Office of Returning Memory, Halven Rook in a room, Orison, or any of the nine final routes; to explain the nine-line mark; to identify the marking on the shard; to name the compartment; to quote a custody number's digits; to put a senior examiner in a room; to ask Sera Mott; to introduce a new antagonist, institution or final enemy; to name the man in a coat; or to move the two objects of nobody's.** **THE WORD *HARBORS* IS ON NO PAGE OF THIS BATCH, INCLUDING INSIDE ANY OTHER WORD.**
6. **It may not be used to obtain, make, release, print, quote, summarize or describe the provisional public copy record; nor to put a seam on a document or on anything else; nor to have any person state what a municipal claim does to a presumed Crown material; nor to produce, obtain, copy or ask for the removed page; nor to be told what was on it; nor to name the commissioned officer who applied for it.** **The three reserved things — the page gone out of a file, the document in which an office accepts a removal, and the phrase *risk management* — ARE ALL SPENT IN THIS BATCH, ON THE NINTH, THE TWELFTH, THE FIFTEENTH AND THE SIXTEENTH OF OCTOBER, AND ONCE SPENT THEY ARE NOT SPENT AGAIN IN MOVEMENTS 4 OR 5. A LATER CHAPTER MAY FIND THE SAME TWO WORDS IN A SECOND DOCUMENT AND MAY NOT PRESENT THAT AS A NEW DISCOVERY.**
7. **It may not be used to read a line of the crew's book aloud in a room, to produce a copy of a record in a room, or to begin the volume's climax.** The book was produced whole in a room on the sixteenth of October and not one line of it was read out of it, and no copy of any record was made in that room, and a schedule was read into the record. **THE READING OF THAT BOOK IN A ROOM IS THE VOLUME'S MIDPOINT AND IS IN CHAPTERS 181 AND LATER.**
8. **It may not be used to take a power stage, or to have a seam settle an argument, prove a motive, convict anybody, or tell Calder what happened.**
9. **It may not be used to pay Bevin Rook's forty marks, to write to him, to go to see him, to ask anybody who has seen him what he said, to reduce the figure, or to hire a boy to read a position back; to pay Mara Venn's forty marks, to pay her six marks and two days, to sign her July finding, to ask her for the line, or to reduce either; to pay the eight shillings and tenpence; to pay the seven pence; to pay the bellwright; to re-write the chandler's note or move any of its three counts; to pay a shilling of the three marks owing; or to make the harbor's poverty better for anything.**
10. **It may not be used to answer the market question of the thirteenth of August, to name a compact, to resolve the coast road, to call it anything, to look at the Kettle, or to produce the reeve's chart. It may not be used to have any office answer, in a room, with a seal on the table, a question this series deliberately left open.**
11. **It may not be used to fuse the lead plug with anything, to fuse the nine fastenings with the nine-line mark, to convert the nine places into the Nine Harbors, or to ask why the three places with no joint are there.**
12. **It may not be used to re-decide the refused license, to pay the thirty marks, or to argue the refusal as a decision this yard is still open on.**
13. **It may not be used to put Mara Venn back on this crew, to pay her, to buy her, to forgive her forty marks, to have the party ask her for anything, or to have the yard go and get her. IT MAY NOT BE USED TO FUSE HER BREAK WITH THE REGISTRY WITH HER LEAVING THIS CREW, WHICH NO CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH DID.**
14. **It may not be used to treat the sheet of the twenty-fifth of August as decided, to withdraw either figure for the bar of gravel, or to have the party put a name on a man who has put a name on a street. Ailsa Rorke was not thanked, not answered and not written to in this batch and the entry of the twenty-seventh of September that this party is not going to put a name on a man who has put a name on a street stands.**
15. **IT MAY NOT BE USED TO LET THE YARD BE TOLD WHAT IS ON LEAF 62 OR LEAF 88, OR TO PUT EITHER LEAF IN THE YARD'S KEEPING, OR TO PRODUCE EITHER, COPY EITHER, OR ASK FOR EITHER BACK.** The page is in a city and is not coming here and the yard has a number and a form and a schedule and a record and a woman it cannot pay, and that is the whole of what it has.

### 8. The costs this batch closes with

1. **A WAGE THAT WAS NOT PAID, on Tuesday the sixth of October, the third Tuesday running, and the count of weeks fallen due with no envelope standing against them is now three.**
2. **FOUR PENCE**, the postage of one letter in the ordinary post, and the whole of what this yard has spent on itself in twenty days, and the bag closes the month four pence lighter than it opened it.
3. **A REFUSAL, IN A LETTERBOX, IN THE HOLDER'S OWN HAND**, and a shipwright who said the shape of that out loud in a shed and was heard, and a man of the first lay who read it in his own wheelhouse and did not know what to do with it for four days.
4. **A DAY OF WORK REFUSED BY THIS YARD**, on Monday the twelfth, a day of about three marks that was there to be taken, and the reason given out loud and it was a bad one and it was a working one.
5. **A DAY OF WORK THAT WAS THERE TO BE BOOKED AND WAS NOT BOOKED**, for a reason of this harbor's and not of this yard's, and not entered as *no work found* because that would be a lie and a flattering one.
6. **A REFUSAL BY A MAN OF FIFTY-ONE IN HIS OWN HAND TO SWEAR TO A FIGURE HE BELIEVES**, and the cost of it falls on the surveyor's entry, which stands with four words in it that this yard never said, and the yard cannot use his letter and did not pay for it and would not be thanked for it.
7. **A CARD IN THE REGISTRY'S OWN HAND WITH TWO WORDS AGAINST ITS OWN REASON**, read by a woman at a copying counter, and a counterfoil in a box under a counter that sat there from the second of September, and a fair copy at a penny a sheet, and a letter in the ordinary post at a penny out of her own pocket, and **five weeks of one woman's not-knowing and five pence of her own money, and the yard paid none of it and could not.**
8. **A LINE REFUSED TWICE**, on the twenty-ninth of September at a figure and at nothing, and again on the twelfth of October on a mole, and the reason given both times, and the price unchanged and not pretended to be payable.
9. **A TRUE SENTENCE ABOUT A PERSON PUT INTO A RECORD IN A CITY**, in eleven words in the holder's own hand, saying there is a woman in this harbor the yard will not name, and it cannot be got off a page, and the party said in a room that it would rather have it than have the record say this harbor produced nothing.
10. **A MAN IN A ROOM NOT ASKING A QUESTION**, and a party still not knowing whether the not-reading of the second column was a rule or an answer, and having entered that it is not going to improve on that entry either.
11. **NINE SENTENCES IN A SHIPWRIGHT'S HEAD THAT ARE NOT ON ANY PAGE**, and a column nobody fills, and the boy's hand at the head of it, and forty marks standing whole.
12. **A TIN CUP ON THE END OF A BENCH**, and a man who did not turn round, and an undertaking against himself that it was done once and is not to be done again.
13. **A MAN SENT DOWN A HILL ONCE** with the truth and nothing else, and a second column line saying that a yard of two and a half people is now the only party in this harbor that a man can come up a hill to and be told no by, and that this is not a thing it did and is not going to be a thing it is proud of. **HE ALSO ASKED A ROOM IN THE MARKET OFFICE ON THE THIRTEENTH AND NOBODY IN THAT ROOM COULD ANSWER HIM, AND HE SAYS HE ASKED IN A DOORWAY ON THE SATURDAY ALSO, AND THE YARD HAS ENTERED THAT IT DID NOT SEE THAT AND IS NOT GOING TO ASK.**
14. **A WORKING HARBOR POORER ON THE TWENTIETH OF OCTOBER THAN ON THE FIRST, AND THE CISTERN WALKED ON NONE OF NINETEEN CHARGES.**

### 9. Proposed canon changes

**None applied to any file outside the four state files. Nine author-level decisions taken on the page, and two prompt figures corrected by the chapters.**

1. **AUTHOR-LEVEL, BINDING — A WOMAN OF THIS HARBOR'S COPYING TRADE, PERNEL SAYE, FIFTY-EIGHT, WITH A COUNTER IN A ROOM OFF THE FISH MARKET**, who copied eleven sheets for the circuit office's copying room on Friday the eighth of September out of the file of the ASTER GANNET, leaf 62, and who keeps withdrawal counterfoils in a box under her counter because a copyist's counterfoil is hers for two years, and who has been up the stairs to that room twice in her life and is not going a third time. **She is the person who made the checkable thing in this batch and she is a working woman and not a device.**
2. **AUTHOR-LEVEL, BINDING — THE WITHDRAWAL COUNTERFOIL AND ITS TWO WORDS**, in the Registry's own hand against its own reason, dated the second of September 2026, on the application of a commissioned officer of the Crown Navy by letter, and the leaf is not to be produced and a copy is held. **THE PHRASE *RISK MANAGEMENT* IS SPENT AND IS ON NO PAGE OF THIS BATCH BEFORE THE NINTH OF OCTOBER.**
3. **AUTHOR-LEVEL, BINDING — LEAF 62 IS THE PAGE A PERSON OF NO OFFICE WROTE ON THE ELEVENTH OF NOVEMBER 2025 AND LEAF 88 IS A PAGE NOBODY HAS SEEN, AND A COPY OF THE FIRST IS TO BE READ WITH THE SECOND.** This is the mechanism by which the Registry uses work of hers: her own refusal, on four grounds, in her own hand, with her trade and a date, is withdrawn from the file, copied, and paired with an account she did not write and has not seen. **A LEAF NUMBER IS NOT A NUMBER ON ANY OBJECT AND NO CUSTODY DIGIT IS QUOTED ANYWHERE IN THIS BATCH.**
4. **AUTHOR-LEVEL, BINDING — MARA VENN'S BREAK WITH THE REGISTRY, IN A LETTER IN THE ORDINARY POST ON SUNDAY THE ELEVENTH OF OCTOBER, IN FOUR LINES, AT A PENNY OUT OF HER OWN POCKET**, and the reason for it: that she has held no office since the fourth of January and cannot stop being a hand in that office's files, and that a letter cannot stop a thing that has already been done and she has written it anyway. **It is a different event from her leaving this crew and no chapter of this batch fuses the two.**
5. **AUTHOR-LEVEL, BINDING — SHE IS NOT COMING TO THE MARKET OFFICE OF THIS TOWN ON A TUESDAY OR A FRIDAY MORNING ANY MORE**, at her own asking, with her own reason, which is not going to be given, and the yard did not arrange it and is not going to un-arrange it. **A man of the first lay came into that room on the thirteenth and asked the room a question about a form with her hand on it, and about nine people in that room could not answer him, and the reader is given the measure of the change in the room and not in a speech.**
6. **AUTHOR-LEVEL, BINDING — A MAN OF THE FIRST LAY OF THIS HARBOR, OSWIN REDE, ABOUT FIFTY**, who asked a room on the thirteenth and the party on the fourteenth, and was sent down the hill by this party once, and said he is not owed anything by this yard. **HIS OWN ACCOUNT OF A SECOND VISIT AND OF A DOORWAY ON THE SATURDAY STANDS AS HIS ACCOUNT AND IS NOT ON A PAGE OF THIS BATCH, AND THE YARD'S BOOK SAYS ONE.**
7. **AUTHOR-LEVEL, BINDING — THE TIN CUP ON THE END OF THE FAR BENCH, ON THE EIGHTEENTH OF OCTOBER**, and the holder's undertaking against himself that it was done once and is not going to be done again, with the reason on the page. **IT IS NOT A FRAGMENT, NOT A REPORT, NOT A SECOND STORY AND NOT A CONFESSION, AND NEITHER BROTHER SAID WHY AND NEITHER BROTHER IS GOING TO.**
8. **AUTHOR-LEVEL, BINDING — A MAN OF THE FIRST LAY, WIL TRANTER, REFUSES A SURVEYOR IN A CITY TO PUT HIS WORD UNDER A LINE ABOUT WATER**, in a letter in his own hand, with his reason in full, and brings it up the hill unasked, and would not take a shilling for it and asked that it be said out loud that the yard offered and he would not have it.
9. **AUTHOR-LEVEL, BINDING — THE YARD'S ANSWER IN A ROOM ON THE SIXTEENTH OF OCTOBER, IN ELEVEN WORDS, IN THE HOLDER'S OWN HAND, READ BACK AND ENTERED**: that there is a person, and that he is not going to give her name and is not going to say that she is in this harbor. **THE COST OF IT IS ON THE PAGE AND THE ENTRY OF THE EIGHTEENTH OF SEPTEMBER THAT THIS PARTY DOES NOT PUT A NAME ON A THING IT CANNOT CHECK IS THE AUTHORITY FOR IT AND IS NOT IMPROVED ON.**

THE THIRD AND THE FOURTH ARE NOW DISTINGUISHED IN ALL FIVE CHAPTERS THAT CARRY THE LINE, AND CHAPTER 172 NO LONGER CALLS THE THIRD OF OCTOBER THE FOURTH. THE SPINE MOVES TWICE IN THIS BATCH AND IT MOVES BECAUSE OF HER AND NOT BECAUSE OF HIM: on the seventeenth of October she said in the shed that she is not going to ask him, and had him enter on one line that she did not ask and that he did not tell, with a reason against the line that is about him.**

and *the delayed note stands at eleven logged occasions and two of them with no call in them* (two); and *twenty-two lines and eighty-eight marks in the wage column, the fifth of March the oldest* (two, being Chapters 178 and 179, and correct in both, and standing only because the review corrected the one place in Chapter 179 that said eighty-four).

**NONE OF THE 33 IS REPAIRED, AND THE REASON IS THE ONE THE VOLUME 03 AUDIT GAVE AT ITS § 21d AND THIS VOLUME'S OWN OUTLINE GIVES AT LOCK L23: the two-column read-out and the standing inventory are how this book states a position, and a harbor that improves on its own phrasing is a different book. THE DEVICE IS ONCE PER BATCH WHERE IT IS A DEVICE — THE READ-OUT, WHICH A MAN USES ON OTHER PEOPLE — AND WAS NOT USED AT ALL IN THIS BATCH. THE INVENTORY IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE SAME THING AND IT RAN IN ALL TEN CHAPTERS OF BATCHES 0001 AND 0002 ALSO.**

**ONE REPEAT WAS REPAIRED UNDER THIS METHOD AND IT IS THE ONE THAT MATTERED: `chapter-0175.md:69` and `chapter-0176.md:51` were a woman of thirty stating the first of her four grounds in twenty-five identical words at a copying counter on the ninth and in a doorway on the twelfth. THE FIRST INSTANCE STANDS EXACTLY AS IT IS AND THE SECOND IS VARIED IN HER OWN WORDS, WITH NO FACT ADDED AND NO FACT REMOVED — WHICH IS THE REMEDY THE VOLUME 03 BATCH 0001 REVIEW ESTABLISHED FOR A DUPLICATED PARAGRAPH, APPLIED HERE TO A DUPLICATED SENTENCE.**

### 11. The shape of the batch, stated on the batch's face

**ALL TEN CHAPTERS CLOSE ON THE STANDING INVENTORY AND THERE IS NO ACTION CHAPTER AND NO TRAINING CHAPTER AND NO RECOVERY CHAPTER IN THE BATCH. That is a fact about the shape of the batch and not a defect in any one of its chapters, and it is recorded here, in the middle of the batch's own account of itself, rather than as a postscript to an audit, because a reader of a movement about a document and a room and a person not being paid should be told plainly that this movement was written in rooms.** Batch 0002 ran the same shape and the reviewer noted it there; the Volume 03 Batch 0001 review had already cut the dominant read-out out of five chapters to break a run of it, and the same remedy is not available here, because in this batch the inventory is not a flourish but the only place a poor yard's whole position is written down at once, and a form about four inches by three is what the batch is about. **What the volume still owes against `outline/volume-04.md` § *Costs this volume may not waive* — at least one injury to a working crew member with a real cost and a real bill, and one bad day — is unpaid in Movements 1, 2 and 3, and is carried forward as standing material and not as this batch's card.**

A reviewer pass over the ten chapters, the four state files and the queued `workspace/volume-04/batch-0004/PROMPT.md` returned FIX with seventeen required continuity and arithmetic items and four prose-and-craft items, and all twenty-one are disposed of below. **VOLUME 04 MOVEMENT 4 IS WRITTEN. Ch181 4,401 · Ch182 3,429 · Ch183 3,672 · Ch184 5,862 · Ch185 3,236 · Ch186 3,006 · Ch187 2,572 · Ch188 3,782 · Ch189 2,983 · Ch190 4,109 — 37,052 words** across ten chapters, Thursday the twenty-second to Tuesday the tenth of November 2026, measured with `wc -w` including headings, against the 2,200–3,200 guideline. **No card file existed for this batch and none was invented; `outline/batches/volume-04-batch-0004.md` is not in this repository, and the batch was shaped out of `outline/volume-04.md` § *Movement 4*, § *Midpoint reversal*, § *Volume climax*, § *Concrete resolution*, § *New-volume question*, § *Final chapter image*, § *Costs this volume may not waive*, § *Reveal discipline for Volume 4* and its thirty locks, and out of the four state files Batch 0003 had just written — the sixth time this series has been built that way.** The volume's midpoint is paid, the movement's ten beats are paid in the order the outline gives them, and no card was cut, no movement boundary was moved, no cost was dropped and no lock was softened. **THE FIGURES IN THIS SENTENCE WERE 36,882 BEFORE THE BATCH 0004 REVIEW'S REPAIRS AND ARE 37,052 AFTER THEM, AND THE REPAIRS THAT MOVED THEM ARE A BORROWED CONFESSION GIVEN BACK TO ITS OWNER, ONE LENGTHENED FIGURE IN A READ-OUT, ONE ATTRIBUTION PUT BACK ON THE RIGHT MAN, THREE SHORT SENTENCES AND FOUR WORDS, AND NO SCENE AND NO BEAT.**

**THE MIDPOINT, IN ONE SENTENCE: a yard of two and a half people read its own crew's book out loud in a room in Morrow Quay for three hours and fifty minutes, whole and unshortened, and in the middle of the second day of it a man who reads joins put one where nobody had put one, on a notice, and it told him that a sheet of paper has been in two hands at two times, and a clerk of the circuit office told the room in the same breath that he had seen the two inks himself since the tenth of September, and the man could not say what it meant, and a market of the eighteenth of July was read out of his own second column in a flat voice by a stranger, and nobody was convicted of anything.**

### 2. The money chain, mark by mark, and where it closes

**A MARK AND TWELVE SHILLINGS in a bag on the evening of Tuesday the twentieth of October, and A MARK AND EIGHT SHILLINGS AND SIXPENCE in it on the evening of Tuesday the tenth of November. A mark is a hundred and sixty pence and a shilling is twelve, so the whole of the arithmetic in this batch hangs on those two figures and both of them are checkable in the prose and both are written out in pence on the page.** **The batch closes forty-two pence lighter than it opened, and the whole of the difference is three shillings and sixpence, and that figure is a bonesetter's bill paid on the twenty-fourth of October and is the only money this yard has spent on itself in twenty-one days.**

No office in this harbor has paid this yard a mark since the eighth of May and none is going to.**

**THE WAGE COLUMN: twenty-three lines and ninety-two marks at the open, twenty-four and ninety-six on the twenty-seventh of October with the wage paid, twenty-four and ninety-six on the third of November with the wage NOT paid and no envelope made, twenty-five and a hundred on the tenth with the wage paid, and the fifth of March the oldest throughout. THREE WAGE TUESDAYS FALL IN THIS BATCH AND ONE OF THEM WAS NOT PAID, being the third of November. THE NUMBER OF WEEKS FALLEN DUE THIS YEAR WITH NO ENVELOPE STANDING AGAINST THEM IS THREE AT THE OPENING OF THIS BATCH AND FOUR AT ITS CLOSE, and all four are entered in the same breath in every place the figure is given, being the fifteenth of August, the fifth of September, the sixth of October and the third of November. THE COUNT OF ENVELOPES ON THE BENCH IN THAT CHEST IS SEVENTEEN AT THE OPENING, EIGHTEEN FROM THE TWENTY-SEVENTH OF OCTOBER, EIGHTEEN THROUGH THE THIRD OF NOVEMBER, AND NINETEEN FROM THE TENTH.**

### 4. Every document and instrument created, quoted, or discovered in this batch

1. **A PAPER OF THE CIRCUIT OFFICE SERVED IN THE DOORWAY OF THE SHED ON FRIDAY THE TWENTY-THIRD OF OCTOBER AT ABOUT A QUARTER TO EIGHT IN THE MORNING, IN ABOUT TWO PEOPLE'S HEARING, BY THE CLERK OF THAT OFFICE, WHO GAVE HIS NAME AND THE NAME OF THAT OFFICE AND DID NOT READ IT OUT OF IT.** It names a day and a room, being **the twenty-eighth and the twenty-ninth of October instant at ten of the morning at the hearing room over the tide-gang store on the west basin.** **THE CONTENTS OF THAT PAPER ARE NOT REPRODUCED IN ANY CHAPTER AND ARE NOT READ ALOUD IN ANY CHAPTER, AND THE HOLDER READ IT HIMSELF AND ENTERED THE DAY AND THE ROOM IN THE FIRST COLUMN WITH THE REASON AGAINST THE LINE.**
2. **A COMMITMENT, IN ABOUT TWO HUNDRED WORDS, GIVEN BY THE HOLDER IN THE DOORWAY ON THURSDAY THE TWENTY-SECOND OF OCTOBER AT ABOUT ELEVEN IN THE MORNING, AND READ BACK AND ENTERED BY THE CLERK:** that the book is to be read whole and unshortened from the first of May to the last page in the order it is in, and that the second column is not a set of facts about this harbor but the only place this party has written down what it could not check, and that the party is not going to leave a line of it out and is not going to soften one. **The clerk's reasons for two things are on the page and neither of them is a third saying of anything said in September or in October.**
3. **A BONESETTER'S FINDING, in a shed, on Friday the twenty-third of October, before anybody had said anything: that it is the bone and not the joint, and that the reader is to say it in that order, and that she wants it in the book in her own hand and not in his.** And her account of the arm on the Saturday: a crack about two inches above the wrist, nothing in the joint out of place, tight for six weeks, not a hand that takes a pump handle in a month, and a quarter of a year.
4. **THE RECORD OF THE SITTING OF THE TWENTY-EIGHTH AND TWENTY-NINTH OF OCTOBER, in a city.** It enters: the attendance and the hour; that the crew's book was produced whole and unshortened and read out by the holder in his own voice and took three hours and fifty minutes; that the clerk asked twice for a thing to be read a second time; **that the third column was not read by the holder and was read by the clerk in a flat voice; that the clerk cannot make that boy come and cannot make anybody ask him; that the holder was asked what a second column is and began an answer and stopped and the answer was entered as not given, and that the same question was put to the ship's hand and answered in one sentence and it was entered that the answer came from her and not from him; that the notice of the tenth of September has been in two hands at two times, with four grounds; that the clerk had that paper since the tenth of September and could see the two inks and entered the fact in that order; that the holder said *I do not know* three times and would not say it a fourth time in a different way; that the entry of the second column of the eighteenth of July and the line of the twenty-third of July were read out and entered; that a page in a book and a sentence in a street are not the same instrument; and that the holder said he said five things in a market on the eighteenth of July and that four are in his book and that the fifth he cannot produce.** **NO COPY OF ANY RECORD WAS MADE IN THAT ROOM AND NONE WAS GIVEN TO ANY PARTY AND NONE WAS ASKED FOR.**
5. **THE NEW STANDARD INSTRUMENT OF THIS BATCH, WHICH IS NOT A DOCUMENT AND IS THE BATCH'S ONLY FINDING: what a clerk can enter.** A line, a date and an hour. **And the reason against a line does not go, and the party worked that out in the shed on Sunday the twenty-fifth of October, before the sitting and not after it, and the clerk gave the same answer in the room in his own trade's words on the first day.** Five checkless lines were going into a record with no reason against any of them, four of them with no name at all, and one of them a line of the fourteenth of August of which the man who wrote it can bring up the first four words.
6. **THE SEAM, ON THE NOTICE OF THE TENTH OF SEPTEMBER, PUT IN A ROOM ON THURSDAY THE TWENTY-NINTH OF OCTOBER, AND IT SAYS ONE THING:** that a sheet of paper has been in two hands at two times. **It does not say which hand is right, or why, or whose the two hands were, and the man who put it there said so in the same breath and would not say more.**
7. **THE BOOK OF HOURS.** Sixteen lines, nine pumps and four boats out and three boats in, over three nights of the thirtieth and thirty-first of October and the first of November, on the mole's steps, with the hour against each and no reason against any of them. **It is the first thing anybody learns about a listening buoy and the party's own second column says that the rest of it needs a crew that keeps the hours, and there is no crew.**

### 7. What this batch may not be used for

**THE METHOD IS THE THREE-PASS ONE THE BATCH 0003 REVIEW LEFT BEHIND, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT COULD HAVE CAUGHT WHAT A BYTE-COMPARISON CANNOT SEE, AND ALL THREE PASSES WERE RUN.**

The first instance stands exactly as it is and the second is varied in the yard's own idiom, with no fact added and no fact removed, and it now carries the one thing the second instance should carry, which is that it is the sixth and last day of the three weeks.**
2. **Pass two — fingerprint and containment.** Every paragraph of twelve words or more, emphasis marks stripped, keyed on its **first forty words**, which catches a truncated copy because the copy and its original share an opening. Then the same set run pairwise for **proper containment**, one paragraph's whole token sequence being a prefix of another's. **PASS TWO, RE-RUN AT THE END OF THE BATCH, RETURNS ZERO FORTY-WORD OPENING MATCHES AND ZERO CONTAINMENT PAIRS INSIDE THE BATCH.** At the first pass, before the repair in pass one, it returned the same single pair; and the containment pass returned nothing at any pass.

### 3. The documents of this batch, one at a time, and what each of them is

1. **THE APPLICATION, Monday the sixteenth of November, one sheet, the holder's own left hand, dated.** Asking the circuit office of this place for a copy of one record of that office, being the record of the entry of one item of recovered transparent mineral in the custody room of that office. It says on the face of it that it asks for a copy of a record and not for the object, that a copy of a record is a thing nobody in this harbor can check, that a party may apply in writing at its own cost for a copy of any record, which grants no copy and makes none and releases nothing, and that no date attaches; and that the release of such a copy is not in this yard's keeping and has never been in it, and that the party is not saying no to it in four years and is not saying yes either. **It is not signed by two hands. A penny of the ordinary post came out of the bag and is entered.**
2. **THE FORM OF THE CIRCUIT OFFICE, Monday the twenty-third of November, brought up the hill by Ambrose Sell, clerk of that office, who gave his name and the name of his office before he said anything.** It states that the application was received on the seventeenth at about ten in the morning and is entered, and that an entry is a line and a date and an hour and grants nothing; that the magistrate of that circuit has directed that a provisional public copy record of the record named by the party be made; that a copy is made at a counter of that office and taken away by the applicant; that when it is made it will carry on its face the limits the record itself carries, printed in the words of the record and not in the words of a clerk; **and that no date attaches to the making of it or to the answering of the application, and the clerk is not able to give one and is not withholding one. AT THE FOOT, WHERE A SIGNATURE WOULD BE IF THE FORM WERE THE SORT OF DOCUMENT THAT HAD ONE, THERE IS THE NAME OF AN OFFICE AND NO MAN'S NAME.**
3. **THE PROVISIONAL PUBLIC COPY RECORD, made at the counter of the copying room of the circuit office on Tuesday the twenty-fourth of November and carried up the hill the same afternoon. Six heads and about a page and a half.** What the sheet is, being a copy of a record and not the thing, and the thing being in the custody room of that office; the item, being one item of recovered transparent mineral, with the number against it not on the sheet; how it came here, being found in water in a bucket in a boat and entered in the keeper's line of a party's own return without being asked, not dried, not wiped, no cloth put into it, sealed by a courier and entered; **the limits the record carries, printed in the record's own words, being that a record of a material is a record of one person's frame and is not a record of a sea, that nothing on the sheet is a finding of consent, and that the sheet is a record of provenance and not of the water; the discrepancy the record carries, being that a manifest referred to in the record, as that manifest stood when that office first entered the item and as that manifest stands now, do not agree, that a line of it has been altered, that the alteration bears a date, and that the record does not show by whose hand, at whose instance or with what intent the alteration was made, and names no person; and what the sheet does not show, being not who altered it, not what the item carried, not who held it before it was in a bucket, not consent, not motive, and not that anything on the sheet is true.** A clerk told the holder three things about a thing leaving a counter, of which the third is that after the first of December nobody in this harbor is going to ask whether this yard wanted it read in a room again. **THE COPY IS DATED THE TWENTY-FOURTH, WHICH IS THE DATE OF THE COUNTER AND NOT THE DATE OF THE RECORD, AND THE YARD PUT THAT DATE THERE ITSELF AND SAYS ON THE PAGE THAT IT KNOWS WHAT IT IS FOR.**
4. **THE ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF THE CIRCUIT OFFICE, Sunday the twenty-ninth of November, half a sheet, no signature anywhere, the name of an office at the foot.** That a manifest referred to in the record of the entry of one item of recovered transparent mineral, as that manifest stood when the office first entered the item and as that manifest stands now, does not agree with a copy of that manifest taken at the time, and that a line of it has been altered and the alteration bears a date; **and that the office does not state by whose hand, at whose instance or with what intent, and names no person; and that the acknowledgment is made because a copy of that record was made, was released and was read out in a room in Morrow Quay, and gives the reason, which is that a copy which has been made cannot be unmade and an office which has released a transcript containing a discrepancy and has not acknowledged it will be read in four years as an office which released it; and that the office does not find against anybody, that this is not a finding of the inquiry, and that the office does not alter the record, the record standing as it stands and the line standing as it stands.** The date at the foot is the date of the acknowledgment and is not the date of the alteration.
5. **THE LETTER, Monday the sixteenth of November, one question, the holder's own left hand, dated, put in the ordinary post at about half past two in the afternoon.** It asks whether this party may offer a part payment on the forty marks out of a day of work and take the rest when there is any. It asks for nothing else, does not ask her to come to this harbor, to be in a room, for a line or for what any record says, and says that if the answer is no then it is no and the yard will enter it with the date and will not ask a second time. **No copy of it went to any office and none will.**
6. **THE ANSWER, dated the twenty-seventh of November, one sheet, thin, folded once with the fold gone soft on it, arriving in the ordinary post on the twenty-eighth, in her own hand. PRICE FIRST, ANSWER SECOND.** The price is that the letter be kept, that what she has written go in the second column with a reason against the line, and that not one word of it go in a market — and the reason is that a sheet on a wall is a sheet, and that in about four years a man in a city is going to read that a yard of Morrow Quay went to a woman it owed forty marks to and asked whether it might pay her part of it and was refused, and that the said reading is going to be true of a man like him and is not going to be true of him, and that there is nothing she can write from where she sits that will make the difference. **The answer is no**, on the ground that a part payment is a receipt and a receipt is a document and a document is how a person of no office becomes a thing a person with an office can use; and that the forty marks stands first after food and has not moved since the fifteenth of October and is not going to move because a yard has had a fortnight; and that the figure of six marks and two days has not moved and is not going to be reduced by anybody including by her, because it is her price and not a debt and the two have never been one thing and this is the first time anybody has tried to make them one; and that this party asked her once in twenty days and is not to ask again this winter, the reason being that a price is a price and the holder asked for one. **THE LETTER SAYS NOT ONE WORD ABOUT THE COPY, THE ROOM, THE SITTING OR THE SHEET, AND THE YARD HAD NOT TOLD HER ABOUT ANY OF THEM AND IS NOT GOING TO, AND THAT IS ENTERED.**
7. **THE FORM OF THE COURT OF WRECK CLAIMS, Friday the fourth of December, half a sheet, no signature anywhere, the name of a court in a city at the head and the name of that court at the foot.** Its five statements are set out in full in `state/current.md` § *The eleven days' new-volume question, and the form that has taken the Second Bell*. **IT IS NOT A SUSPENSION, NOT A PENALTY AND NOT A FINDING AGAINST ANYBODY, AND IT SAYS THAT A PERSON WHO IS NOT EXAMINED IS NOT A PERSON WHO HAS BEEN REFUSED. IT EXPRESSLY DOES NOT TOUCH THE SECOND SEASON OF THE WRIT, AND IT STATES THAT THE COURT HAS NOT CONSIDERED THE WRIT AND TAKES NO NOTICE OF IT. A COPY OF THE SAID RECORD IS TO BE PRODUCED TO THAT COURT ON THE FOURTH DAY OF JANUARY.**

**A mark is a hundred and sixty pence and a shilling is twelve, so a wage of four marks is 640p, a day that brought four marks is 640p, a day that brought three marks is 480p, two shillings is 24p, and a penny is a penny. The whole of what came into this yard in twenty-one days is seven marks and forty-eight pence and the whole of what went out is six marks and twenty-five pence, and the net is four hundred and fifty-five pence, and Chapter 200 says the whole of the difference in its own words: two days of work on a hirer's own account, two shillings to a bonesetter, one wage and a penny of postage. NO FIGURE IN THE BAG AT ANY POINT IN THIS BATCH EXCEEDS SIX MARKS AND EIGHT SHILLINGS. NO OFFICE IN THIS HARBOR PAID THIS YARD A MARK AND NONE IS GOING TO. NO DAY OF WORK WAS BOOKED ON THE FIFTEENTH, THE EIGHTEENTH, THE TWENTY-SECOND, THE TWENTY-SEVENTH, THE TWENTY-EIGHTH, THE TWENTY-NINTH, THE SECOND OR THE THIRD, AND EVERY ONE OF THOSE DAYS IS ENTERED IN THE FIRST COLUMN WITH THE REASON AGAINST THE LINE.**

**The wage column: twenty-five lines and one hundred marks at the open; twenty-six lines and one hundred and four marks on the twenty-fourth with the wage paid; unchanged at twenty-six and a hundred and four on the first of December with the wage not paid and no envelope made. The fifth of March the oldest throughout. Envelopes on the bench: nineteen, then twenty, then twenty. The number of weeks fallen due this year with no envelope standing against them is FOUR at the open, FIVE after the seventeenth of November and SIX after the first of December, and all six are given in the same breath in every place the figure appears. The bag was 379p short of the wage on the seventeenth and 403p short of it on the first of December and both figures are on the page.**

### 5. The people, and the four who are not in a room

- **Calder Marr, thirty-two.** No water on any day of this batch. He applies, he reads a page and a half in a shed, he goes into a room and is not the one who reads it, he says no to the item and says he wants it, he is asked about the water and says he cannot vouch for it, he is refused by a letter, he is refused twice in a market and gives the reason, he says the note is not re-written for the third time in seven months, and on the fourth of December he loses the eligibility he wanted before the writ and enters that the release was the party's own doing and that the party is not going to call the cost somebody else's. **THE NOT-TELLING OF THE SEVENTH OF AUGUST IS NOW SIX ENTRIES AND A SIXTH OCCASION NOT TO AND IS NOT PAID, AND THE REASON OF THE FOURTH OF OCTOBER IS GIVEN AGAIN WITH THE UNDERTAKING NOT TO INVENT A SECOND ONE.**
- **Nessa Pike, twenty-seven.** Her strapping came off on the twenty-first of November, two shillings, paid into the bonesetter's own hand at her own counter. The strapping-off visit is the END of the injury paid in Movement 4 and is not a second injury, and no new bill is charged against her and no new cost is taken in this batch. **She said in a bonesetter's room that the bone knitted straight and that the wrist does not turn all the way round in a cold month for two years and that the only thing that makes it worse is a boat on a cold tide with a fall in the hand, and that she does not want it in her own book. She entered in her own hand that until the first of March this yard is a party of one and a half and not two, and that every day this yard books in this month is a day it books with a man in it. She read the copy out in a room in six heads. She wrote the eleven-line list of what is not going into the room. SHE HAS NOT BEEN THANKED AND IS NOT GOING TO ASK AND HE HAS NOT THANKED HER AND IS NOT GOING TO.**
- **Mara Venn, thirty.** Not in this harbor, not in a room, not asked for anything but one thing, which was answered in writing. **SHE PRICED IT AND THE ANSWER WAS NO, AND THE PRICE IS ON THE PAGE, AND NEITHER IS IMPROVED ON. She is not on the crew, is not of the yard, is not a holder, is not on the four names, is owed forty marks first after food, and the reporting clause on the writ of the first of May does not reach her and never did. No chapter of this batch fused the ask with the copy, with the room, with the sitting, with the sheet or with her being used by an office, and no chapter has her break with the Registry, and she did not come back to this crew and was not asked to.**
- **Ors Kest, forty-four.** Appears once, in the open air, on the nineteenth of November, at the foot of the mole's steps, in about eleven people's hearing. **THE YARD ASKED HIM FOR A ROOM AND A DAY AND NOT FOR AN INSTRUMENT, AND SAID SO FIRST, AND SAID THAT THE NINTH ACKNOWLEDGEMENT IS SPENT AND A TENTH MAY NOT BE ENTERED AND WAS NOT ASKED FOR, AND SAID THAT THE POWER TO SEAT ONE OF TWO DISPUTANTS BELONGS TO THE INQUIRY AND NOT TO THE WRIT AND THAT THE TWO INSTRUMENTS ARE NOT THE SAME INSTRUMENT. HE NAMED THE PRICE OUT LOUD BEFORE HE SAID YES: one morning of one man of the tide gang, whom he refused to name because the moment he names him he is a man in this business, and the tide gang is four men short and will be four men short at the first of March. THE PRICE DID NOT FALL ON THE THIRD LAY'S FOUR DAYS AND NOT ON A MAN OF THE FIRST LAY'S MONDAY AND NOT ON FENN ARDLE'S TUESDAY.** He said his ledger is spent, that his office cannot pay for a clerk's day and owes him one, and that he is not a friend of this party and has never said he was.
- **Ambrose Sell, clerk of the circuit office.** Named wherever a clerk of that office appears, in Chapters 194 and 196. He came up the hill with a form and said three things, one of which is that no date attaches; he read the yard's eleven-line list back twice and said he had not asked about any of the eleven; he took the chair at the end of the table in a room, entered the date and the hour and the place before he said anything, entered on the first line of the record that the office is not sitting to decide anything and finds against nobody, gave the reading to the ship's hand and not to the holder, put the question about the item in his own words, and put the question about the water in his own words and read the answer back and entered all of it. **HE SAID NEITHER OF THE TWO THINGS HE SAID IN SEPTEMBER AND OCTOBER A THIRD TIME, HE DID NOT NAME THE MAGISTRATE, AND THE NAME OF THE MAN IN A COAT IS ON NO PAGE OF THIS BATCH.**
- **Hessa Barlow, forty-four, a bonesetter.** The strapping came off on the twenty-first and she charged two shillings and said why it is not the figure of the twenty-fourth of October, and said a visit on the fourteenth day is a look and not a visit, and said the good of it and the rest of it, and would not be thanked.
- **Pernel Saye, fifty-eight, a copyist with a counter in a room off the fish market open to anybody from eight until the market is off the boards, where a sheet is a penny and forty sheets a shilling.** Took the acknowledgment up in the market on the thirtieth of her own account and unasked, made twenty-one copies at about nine minutes a sheet, and read the whole form out at the head of the fish dock on the first of December in about forty people's hearing in about nine minutes. **SHE WAS NOT PAID BY THIS YARD, THIS YARD DID NOT ASK HER, DID NOT SEND ANYBODY AND DID NOT STAND NEAR HER WHILE SHE DID IT, AND SHE SAID SHE WOULD RATHER THEY DID NOT COME AND STAND BY HER.**
- **Wil Tranter, fifty-one, of the first lay, master of a coaster of about a hundred and ninety tons of his own.** Asked two questions in a market on the second of December and was refused twice with the same reason. **HE SAID HE WAS THE ONE ASKING AND THAT THE TWO THINGS ARE NOT THE SAME THING.**
- **Denzil Hare, of the third lay, about fifty, a boat of his own and no crew of his own since the spring.** Asked whether the case of five bells is coming up, in a market, and was told the truth about it and that it is not on anybody's book.
- **Alden Marr, sixty-one. AT THE FAR BENCH ON FOUR DAYS OF THIS BATCH — Monday the sixteenth and Thursday the nineteenth of November, Wednesday the twenty-fifth of November, and Thursday the third of December — and on no other day of the twenty-one,** not asked for anything on any of the four and asking nothing on any of the four, and Calder Marr did not go over to him on any of the four. **THE FIGURE OF FOUR IS COUNTED FROM THE PROSE AND WRITTEN FROM THE COUNT, WHICH IS THE RULE THE BATCH 0002 REVIEW LEFT AFTER TWO FAR-BENCH FIGURES HAD TO BE CORRECTED AGAINST THE CHAPTERS. NO FRAGMENT, NO REPORT TALK, NO SECOND STORY, NO CONFESSION, AND THE TIN CUP OF THE EIGHTEENTH OF OCTOBER IS NOT REPEATED.**

Magister Ilya Serr is on no page of this batch at all, in a room or out of one. The man in a coat of an office in a city is not named and is not in this batch.**

### 6. The eleven-line list, and the batch's one working rule

**ON SUNDAY THE TWENTY-SECOND OF NOVEMBER THE SHIP'S HAND WROTE ON A SHEET OF THIS YARD'S OWN PAPER A LIST OF ELEVEN THINGS THAT ARE NOT GOING INTO THE ROOM OF THE HEARING ROOM OVER THE TIDE-GANG STORE, AND IT WAS READ OUT IN THE SHED AND THE HOLDER WROTE IT INTO THE FIRST COLUMN IN HIS OWN LEFT HAND WITH THE DATE ON IT, AND NEITHER OF THEM ADDED TO IT AND NEITHER OF THEM TOOK ANYTHING OFF IT.** The eleven are: the place of the case of five bells; the four people it belongs to; the limit they wrote themselves; the plate at the fifth seam; the two objects on the crown of this mole; the boy; the forty marks standing whole to him; the forty marks first after food to a person of no office; the delay; a letter this yard is expecting in the ordinary post on the Saturday; and the two figures for the bar of gravel together with the Kettle, which was not looked at. **A clerk of the circuit office read the list back twice in the shed and said he had not asked about any of the eleven and was not going to, and gave the reason, which is that a clerk reads a page and does not go and look for the eleventh line of a yard's book. The holder stopped the woman at the ninth item and made a tenth of it, which is the letter, and the reason is on the page, and the second column says it is not there because a line about a person of no office in a room is a document about her and she has been in a record in a city since the sixteenth of October without anybody asking her.**

The bare fact is carried once, in the second column of Chapter 195, with a reason, and without a name. **THE FOUR LINES ABOVE THE NAMED LINE OF THE TWENTIETH OF JULY ARE STILL FOUR, ARE STILL NAMELESS, ARE NOT STRUCK OUT, AND A REQUEST TO STRIKE A LINE OUT OF A COLUMN IS REFUSED IN THE SAME WORDS IT IS REFUSED FOR A LINE IN ANY COLUMN.**
2. **It may not be used to ask the bellwright, to print a digit of anything he said on the second of July, or to open the chest.** He is in no chapter of it as a person and the chest was not opened and was not brought down the hill.
3. **It may not be used to enter a tenth acknowledgement, to lift, narrow, re-serve or alter the notice of the thirty-first, to reopen the eight-clause plan of the seventeenth of January, to reach the plate at the fifth seam, to close the plate note, to widen the writ's ground, to add a fifth name, to manufacture a second season, to name the man of Ashtide, to ask him anything, or to put a person, boat or lead of this yard inside the first clause of that notice on any day.**
4. **It may not be used to make a fifth return, to move the counting rule, to report the work of any day to any office, or to confuse the inquiry's power to seat one of two disputants with the writ's power. A ROOM IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT AND THE NINTH ACKNOWLEDGEMENT IS SPENT.**
5. **It may not be used to name the Nine Harbors as a compact, the Quietening, the Crown Seal, the Office of Returning Memory, Halven Rook in a room, Orison, or any of the nine final routes; to explain the nine-line mark; to name the compartment or to restate its finding; to quote a custody number's digits; to put a senior examiner in a room; to ask Sera Mott; to introduce a new antagonist, institution or final enemy; to name the man in a coat; or to move the two objects of nobody's. THE WORD *HARBORS* IS ON NO PAGE OF THIS BATCH, INCLUDING INSIDE ANY OTHER WORD, AND THE PHRASE *RISK MANAGEMENT* IS ON NO PAGE OF THIS BATCH AT ALL.**
6. **IT MAY NOT BE USED TO PUT A SECOND SEAM ON A DOCUMENT, TO HAVE A SEAM SAY MORE THAN IT SAYS, TO HAVE A SEAM SETTLE AN ARGUMENT OR PROVE A MOTIVE, OR TO READ A LINE OF THE CREW'S BOOK ALOUD IN A ROOM AGAIN AS AN EVENT. THE READING OF THAT BOOK IN A ROOM HAPPENED ONCE, ON THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF OCTOBER, AND IT IS PAID, AND THE ONE SEAM WAS PUT ON THE TWENTY-NINTH AND IT IS PAID, AND NEITHER IS REPEATED AND A SEARCH OF THE TEN CHAPTERS FOR *SEAM* RETURNS ONLY THE PHRASE *THE FIFTH SEAM*.**
7. **IT MAY NOT BE USED TO TAKE A POWER STAGE, TO RE-TAKE, IMPROVE OR NAME THE FAULTREADER STAGE, OR TO PUT A BELLWRIGHT, KEELWRIGHT, STORM-READER, CHORUS DIVER OR OPENHAND STAGE ON THE PAGE. THE BOOK OF HOURS IS THE FIRST THING AND NOT THE TRADE, IT WAS NOT EXTENDED, AND THE REST OF IT NEEDS A CREW.**

9. **It may not be used to answer the market question of the thirteenth of August in any new way, to name a compact, to resolve the coast road, to call it anything, to look at the Kettle, or to produce the reeve's chart. IT MAY NOT BE USED TO HAVE ANY OFFICE ANSWER, IN A ROOM, WITH A SEAL ON THE TABLE, A QUESTION THIS SERIES DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN.**
10. **IT MAY NOT BE USED TO LET THE YARD BE TOLD WHAT IS ON LEAF 62 OR LEAF 88, OR TO PUT EITHER LEAF IN THE YARD'S KEEPING, OR TO PRODUCE EITHER, COPY EITHER, OR ASK FOR EITHER BACK. IT MAY NOT BE USED TO COUNT THE NINE SENTENCES, ASK FOR THEM, OR HAVE ANYBODY WRITE DOWN WHAT THE SHIPWRIGHT SAID IN A DOORWAY, AND THE SHIPWRIGHT'S TWO REFUSALS OF THE TWENTY-FOURTH AND TWENTY-FIFTH OF OCTOBER STAND AND NEITHER IS REVERSED.**

IT MAY NOT BE USED TO HAVE HIM TELL HER AND BE A RELIEF, A PRICE, AN EXCHANGE, OR A THING THAT BUYS ANYTHING.**

THE FORM ITSELF SAYS THE OPPOSITE OF ALL FOUR AND THE FORM IS THE AUTHORITY.**
13. **IT MAY NOT BE USED TO SHOW A MAN IN A CITY PRODUCING THE COPY RECORD, TO PUT ANY OFFICE IN VEYR IN A ROOM ANSWERING A QUESTION ABOUT AN OFFICE'S OWN HISTORY, TO SAY WHAT THE MAN IN THE COURT'S FORM THINKS THE GROWNTH-THREE-HUNDRED-YEAR RECORD-KEEPING WAS FOR, OR TO ANSWER THE NEW-VOLUME QUESTION IN ANY DIRECTION AT ALL.**

2. **A BONESETTER'S TWO SHILLINGS ON THE TWENTY-FIRST, the only money this yard has spent on a person in twenty-one days, and a quarter of a year out of the left side of a shipwright standing untouched and unasked after the strapping came off.**
