### 4. The four records, one at a time, and every other document of this batch

**THE FOUR RECORDS ARE NAMED HERE AS THEY STAND ON THE PAGE, AND A LATER CHAPTER MAY NOT CHANGE ANY WORD OF THIS LIST. THEY ARE FOUR OF THE NINE RECORDS NINE COMMUNITIES KEEP, ONE IN EACH, THEY ARE INCOMPATIBLE, ALL FOUR OF THEM ARE TRUE, AND THE INCOMPATIBILITY IS THE FINDING. NONE OF THEM IS A COPY OF ANYTHING BUT THE FOURTH, AND THE FOURTH IS A COPY OF A THING THIS YARD HAS NEVER SEEN.**

1. **THE FIRST OF THE FOUR, LENT, AND IT IS A PAGE THAT IS NOT A COPY OF ANYTHING AND IS NOT A DOCUMENT ANYBODY SENT ANYWHERE AND IS SIMPLY THE PAGE A PLACE HAS AT THE INSIDE OF A BAR.** One sheet of ruled paper about the size of a board, folded once across, with the fold at the left edge a tear and not a stitch, torn out of a thing that was never bound and carried four hundred miles in a boat's locker under a coil of warp. Three hands: two about thirty years apart by the iron in the ink, and a third four years old which is the hand of the man of the second lay's own bosun, who signed it at the foot because a bosun writes his name. The line that matters: **the ninth, and a hard night, and the light on the point was burning, and two boats came in on it about two in the morning and lay there till it was light.** It also carries a line in the third hand, four years old, being that a boat of about sixty tons came in on the tide and was not asked where she was from and that somebody on a wall said a thing about that which is not written down because whoever wrote it did not want to write it. **It came out of the locker of a man of the second lay with a boat of about seventy tons, in a piece of oilcloth, on Monday the eighteenth of January, and he said on his way down that he had not looked inside the oilcloth and did not want to, and it went down that hill with him on the Tuesday afternoon of the twenty-sixth and this yard was told nothing about what had been said about it.**
2. **THE SECOND OF THE FOUR, PRODUCED BY A WOMAN OF SEVENTY-ONE WHO HAS KEPT A PAGE IN A HOUSE FOR FORTY YEARS AND HAS NEVER BEEN ASKED FOR IT, AND WHO CAME UP THE HILL UNASKED.** One sheet folded once, the fold a crease and not a tear, about forty lines in three hands, and the top of the fold worn to a channel. The line that matters, in her grandmother's hand and the oldest on the sheet: **the ninth, and a hard night, and there was no light on the point, and the man that keeps it had the lamp out the week before and the oil was not carried, and the two boats that came in were in before it was light and were not in on the light.** It also carries, in her mother's hand, a sale of the right to take what came ashore, to a man from the town two days down this coast, for a sum written out in words and not in figures, **and the words do not add up to the figures**, witnessed by four men of whom three were of that place; and that page went out of that house twice in her lifetime, both times to men from a city and both times for work they did not do there, and came back both times. **She came up the mole on foot on Saturday the sixteenth of January and stood at the door for about a minute and said she was not answering a knock, and left it on the bench until the Tuesday and took it home at about four on the twenty-sixth, and asked no question about the reading and told this yard beforehand that she did not want to be told about it afterwards and did not want a copy, and that house is one of four within thirty yards and three of the other three have a front door that faces it.**
3. **THE THIRD OF THE FOUR, SHOWN, AND CARRIED NINE YEARS OUT OF THE PLACE IT IS ABOUT IN A MAN'S OWN BOOK.** The fourth page of the ninth leaf of a book of two hundred and six leaves that a man of sixty-four of the first lay began when he was seventeen and has never shown to anybody, in a town four days up this coast. Not a copy of anything; no office has ever had it and no clerk has ever seen it. The line, in a hand that is not his and is not his father's: **on a Tuesday in a bad month, a man of that place, aged thirty-one, went out in a boat of about sixty tons, and the tide was making at about six in the evening, and he did not come back, and there was a lantern in his pocket and a boot knife and two shillings and sixpence, and his mother held his things and his brother held the boat, and the boat came back and he did not.** **It is the only one of the four that is about one person and the only one of the four that has been moved out of its place, and the fourth of the four forbids both, and the man of sixty-four said before anybody else that a boat of about sixty tons in the first page and in this one is two boats and is not going to be made into one.**
4. **THE FOURTH OF THE FOUR, WHICH IS THE NINTH OF THE NINE, WHICH CAME UP THIS HILL IN A CRATE OF CHALK OUT OF A PLACE TWO DAYS DOWN THIS COAST ON THE TUESDAY BOAT, AND WHICH IS A RECORD OF AN AGREEMENT ABOUT A PAGE, AND WHICH CARRIES A NAME. IT IS A SHEET FOLDED TWICE WITH THE FOLD A FOLD AND NOT A TEAR, IT IS A COPY AND NOT THE THING, AND THIS YARD KNOWS IT IS A COPY BECAUSE THE WRITING IS EVEN ALL THE WAY DOWN THE PAGE AND BECAUSE THE INK ON THE UPPER TWO THIRDS IS A DIFFERENT MAKE FROM THE INK ON THE LOWER THIRD. THERE IS NO DATE ON IT AND NO NUMBER ON IT AND NO SEAL AND NO STAMP AND NO SIGNATURE AND NO OFFICE NAMED ANYWHERE ON IT.** At the head of it, in a hand bigger than the rest and with a space under it, is a name. **THE NAME IS *THE NINE HARBORS*. IT IS WRITTEN ONCE, IN CHAPTER 225, IN THE MOUTH OF THE SHEET, AND IT IS NOWHERE ELSE IN THE WHOLE OF VOLUME 05, INCLUDING INSIDE THE SAME CHAPTER, WHERE THE TWO OF THEM REFER TO IT AFTERWARDS ONLY AS THE NAME AT THE HEAD OF THE FOURTH OF THE FOUR.** **IT IS A NAME OF AN AGREEMENT AND NOT OF A NAME OF A BODY, AND THERE IS NO BODY IN IT, AND NOTHING ON THAT SHEET SAYS THAT NINE PLACES EVER MADE ONE THING OF THEMSELVES OR EVER DID ANYTHING AGAIN AFTER THE DAY IT WAS WRITTEN, AND THE SHEET DOES NOT SAY THAT THE AGREEMENT HELD AND THIS YARD IS NOT GOING TO SAY IT EITHER.** Under the name: an agreement made at a place, between nine, concerning a page. Four of the lines are legible and two are not, and what there is says: that a page about a place is the place's; and that it is not to be carried out of the place it is about; and that a copy is not a page and has none of a page's standing; and that no one of the nine is to be asked what another of the nine keeps. **At the foot, in a second ink, in a hand of that same place, later, and not one of the four lines: that a page was carried out of that place in a year nobody wrote down, and was brought back in another year, and has been kept ever since in a house that is not the house it was kept in before. IT DOES NOT SAY THE CARRYING WAS WRONG.** It went down this coast on Saturday the thirtieth of January in the inside of a man's coat and not in his barrow.

**AND THE OTHER DOCUMENTS OF THIS BATCH, one at a time, and none of them is one of the four:**

5. **NINE PLACES, IN A LIST IN THE SHIPWRIGHT'S HAND, CARRIED IN THIS YARD'S OWN BOOK SINCE THE MONTH OF OCTOBER PAST, READ ALOUD AT THE TOP OF THE BENCH ON SATURDAY THE THIRTIETH OF JANUARY: this harbor's own weir; the inside of the bar; the other side of the water; the point with the light; a place four days up this coast; a place two days down this coast; the next town down this coast; the hard at Ashtide; and Lowfen, a chain of reed islands and floating markets two days out. THEY ARE PLACES AND THE LIST DOES NOT SAY WHAT IS KEPT AT ANY OF THEM AND NEVER HAS. THE OTHER FIVE OF THE NINE ARE THIS HARBOR'S OWN WEIR, THE POINT WITH THE LIGHT, THE NEXT TOWN DOWN THIS COAST, THE HARD AT ASHTIDE AND LOWFEN.** Lowfen is entered for the first time in this volume and is entered as a place with people living on the water and not as a route name.
6. **A SHEET OF PAPER BOUGHT AT A COUNTER OFF THE FISH MARKET ON THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF JANUARY FOR ONE PENNY, ON WHICH THE SHIPWRIGHT WROTE THE SIX TITLES OF THE FIVE PIECES OF PAPER, AND WHICH WENT INTO THE BOOK ON THE THIRD OF FEBRUARY AND DID NOT COME OUT.**
7. **A CORNER OF THE SHEET AND A HALF, ABOUT THREE INCHES OF IT, GONE IN THE SHIPWRIGHT'S HAND ON SUNDAY THE THIRTY-FIRST OF JANUARY ALONG THE FOLD THAT HAD BEEN GOING SOFT SINCE THE FOURTEENTH. IT CANNOT BE PUT BACK.**
8. **NOTHING ANSWERED.** The answer to the printer's letter of the twentieth of December is in this yard's drawer and this yard is not going to send it, and the reason is in the first column because a man in this town can get on the coach and ask that printer whether this yard has written to him.

### 5. The dated positions at the end of Chapter 230

- **The slate wall behind the reeve's bench came down bare three times in this batch, all Mondays, all with the clerk keeping his own page and not mentioning it, and no sitting was held on any of them: Monday the eighteenth of January being the thirty-seventh Monday since the first of May, Monday the twenty-fifth the thirty-eighth, and Monday the first of February the thirty-ninth. THE COUNTER DID NOT RESTART.**
- **The cistern behind the engine house was charged at no figure by four men this yard does not know on five rota days in twenty days — the eighteenth, twenty-first, twenty-fifth and twenty-eighth days of January instant and the first day of February next — and this party walked none of them. THE WALK IS NIL AND IT STAYS NIL, AND THAT IS THE SEVENTEENTH OF THE CHARGES THIS PARTY HAS ENTERED WALKED ON NONE OF SINCE THE THIRD DAY OF AUGUST PAST. The charge of the ninth day of November stands entered with no figure against it, and the next rota day is the fourth of February and is past the end of this batch.**
- **The far bench is entered in ALL TEN OF THE CHAPTERS OF THIS BATCH AND IT COVERS ALL TWENTY DAYS, at two instances to the chapter except in Chapter 229, which carries the occupied line and the unoccupied line together in the first column. THE FIGURES OF *NINE OF THE TEN CHAPTERS* AND OF *EIGHTEEN OF THE TWENTY DAYS* ARE WITHDRAWN: THEY WERE WRITTEN FROM THE SUMMARY AND NOT FROM THE CHAPTERS, AND EVERY ONE OF THE TEN CHAPTERS CARRIES THE ENTRY. IT WAS NOT OCCUPIED AT ANY HOUR ON THE FIFTEENTH, SIXTEENTH, SEVENTEENTH, NINETEENTH, TWENTIETH, TWENTY-FIRST, TWENTY-SECOND, TWENTY-THIRD, TWENTY-FOURTH, TWENTY-SEVENTH, TWENTY-EIGHTH, TWENTY-NINTH, THIRTIETH AND THIRTY-FIRST DAYS OF JANUARY INSTANT, NOR ON THE SECOND AND THIRD DAYS OF FEBRUARY NEXT, AND EVERY ONE OF THOSE LINES IS ENTERED WITH NO FIGURE OF WHAT CAME BEFORE IT, AND THE SEVENTEEN-WORD TAIL OF THAT LINE IS NOW VARIED IN THE YARD'S OWN IDIOM IN EVERY CHAPTER AFTER 221, 221 BEING THE FIRST INSTANCE OF THE BATCH. IT WAS OCCUPIED ON MONDAY THE FIRST DAY OF FEBRUARY NEXT FROM ABOUT TEN UNTIL ABOUT FOUR. NOT ASKED FOR ANYTHING ON ANY DAY, ASKING NOTHING ON ANY DAY, NO FRAGMENT, NO REPORT TALK, NO SECOND STORY, AND CALDER MARR DID NOT GO OVER TO HIM ON ANY DAY OF THE TWENTY.**
- **The two objects of nobody's are about two hundred and thirty-five days up the crown of that mole at the end of Chapter 230, about nine feet apart, under two tarpaulins, one with a corner off it since the seventeenth of June and not lashed back, and neither has moved. The sequence across the ten chapters is 217, 219, 221, 223, 225, 227, 229, 231, 233 and 235, two a chapter, each chapter keying its figure to its last day. THE FIGURE IS STATED ONCE IN EACH OF THE TEN CHAPTERS AND NOT TWICE IN ANY OF THEM. The party went past both of them once in these twenty days, on no day this batch names, and touched neither.**
- **The notice of the thirty-first of October has its four clauses and has not been lifted, narrowed, re-served or altered, and no person, no boat and no lead of this yard went inside its first clause on any day of the twenty. The plate at the fifth seam is in eleven feet in this mole's own foundation stone, seen and not measured and not touched, THE NOTE AGAINST IT STANDS OPEN, and no better letter was written about it in three weeks. The custody room was not asked for, nothing came out of it, no digit of any of the three numbers is in this yard's book, and the question that no paper in this harbor or in that office's copying room answers was not put to anybody. The lead plug is not asked about, not printed, not opened and not brought down the hill. The glass storm is not referred to. The run under this town is not referred to. The compartment is not named and no step of its finding is restated. The custody-log re-entry of the twentieth of December gave no reason and is not referred to.**
- **The delayed note stands at eleven logged occasions and two of them with no call in them, nothing was entered in these twenty days and nothing was measured, the delay is a hand's width of a second and has not moved, and nobody in this harbor has ever said why. No Volume 05 chapter may name the call, and none of these ten does.**
- **There are four returns up this coast and there is no fifth, and no day of this batch produced a finding of worked glass and no return of any kind was made. The plate, the boy, the third column, the five bells, the delay, the custody items, the lead plug, the coast road, the harbor's poverty and the three of the four Gannet documents are all exactly where Batch 0002 left them.**
- **The harbor is poorer at the close of this batch than at its open.** One herring berth of two is out, the north berth is out, the mole-head light is not on because a light costs oil, the fire party's hose is dead until the spring, the tide gang is four men short, the hard at Ashtide is unanswered, the cistern is charged at no figure on five rota days and walked on none, the compressor's gland is unpaid and useless and the thing after the gland is the hose and this harbor has no hose and no figure has been put on the hose, nineteen winters are in a list being made up in a city by a woman at a table who has this yard's four returns in her hands, a boat of forty tons is a hand short since the middle of July, a man of thirty-four is sixty pounds short in a month he has not put on anybody, and a sheet and a half that came up that hill on foot is in the palm of a woman's hand in pieces. **NOTHING THIS YARD DID IN THESE TWENTY DAYS HAS MADE ANYTHING BETTER AND NO FIGURE IN THIS HARBOR IS THE PRICE OF ANY OF IT.**

### 6. The people, and the four who are not in a room

- **Calder Marr, thirty-two.** He went to four households in two days and asked to see a page. He read a page of a place at the inside of a bar and did not look at it for an hour and a quarter. He was asked a question by a man of sixty-four and could not answer it. He read the name at the head of the fourth of the four out loud twice to one other person and did not write it in this yard's book. He spent two hours at the top of a bench with four pages of other people's and no third person in the room. **On the twenty-seventh he read his own first column out loud and found it to be a line of custody with a name at the end of every line and four gaps in it, and said that it is the first thing about his own method he has not been able to see because it was inside it, and that was right. On the twenty-eighth he bought a sheet of paper at a counter and asked a question he could not answer himself. On the thirty-first he laid out the five pieces of paper this yard holds to look for one word and a corner of one of them came off in the ship's hand. On the third of February he wanted to write to a printer and did not.** **THE ONE NAMING OF THE CONDITION IS NOT IN THIS BATCH AND WAS NOT AVAILABLE.**
- **Nessa Pike, twenty-seven, a party of one and a half until the first of March.** She read the first of the four and stopped twice on one line and would not say why. She wrote the cost of a day lost in the second column with no name in it. She heard the second of the four out loud from a woman of seventy-one and did not say which of the two is wrong. She said the sentence a woman of seventy-one said about a page and did not improve on it. **She counted the nines and found four of them and said that this yard has treated them as one thing for a year because a number is a number. She found the fifth thing with a pencil in her hand and invented no dates. She asked for four lines to be struck out of the first column and was refused in the same words it is refused for a line in any column, and said that was the whole of what she had to say and sat down. She did not tell the copyist what a second column is and gave the reason herself.** **SHE HAS NOT BEEN THANKED AND IS NOT GOING TO ASK, AND HE HAS NOT THANKED HER AND IS NOT GOING TO AND DID NOT.**
- **Pernel Saye, fifty-eight, a copyist with a counter in a room off the fish market.** One scene, on Thursday the twenty-eighth of January, at about eleven. **She was asked one question she had never been asked at that counter in four months — a record a man can check, or a record nobody can check, which is worth having — and she refused it, and gave the nearest thing to it she has, and said before she said it that it is about her and not about their page and is not to be written down as an answer.** Three things: that she can price the making of a page and the keeping of a page, which is nothing, and cannot price the being right about it, and that nobody on this coast can price the being right about it and anybody who says he can is selling a book or a room or a good; that the making of a thing is her whole trade and she has never once been asked about the other half of it and did not know there was an other half until about three years ago; and that a record a man can check is worth what the man is who checks it and a record nobody can check is worth what the person who keeps it is worth, and that those are not the same figure and there is no figure for either, and that she has met about nine people in thirty-one years she would trust with a page and about four hundred she would not, and that the nine are not better than the four hundred and are just nine. **SHE WAS NOT TOLD WHAT A SECOND COLUMN IS, SHE DID NOT ASK, AND THE REASON IS ON THE PAGE: the moment a man tells a woman what a column is he is selling her a thing, and she has told this party to their faces that she can tell the difference between a thing a man is selling and a thing a man is showing. SHE WAS CHARGED ONE PENNY FOR A SHEET OF PAPER AND SOLD NOTHING, AND NO OTHER MONEY OF THIS WARD WENT INTO THAT ROOM.** She has not been told what the yard's turn is, she is not a villain, she is not on a ladder, and she said the other thing she has not looked at in thirty-one years is still coming and will be worse than anything she said that day.
- **A man of sixty-four of the first lay, a joiner from a place four days up this coast, in this harbor on a job, with a book of his own begun when he was seventeen and never shown to anybody.** Four visits: the Friday the fifteenth at the boards, showing one leaf; the Monday the eighteenth with that leaf left on the bench, when he would not let his hand off it and read the line himself; the Tuesday the twenty-sixth at four, to collect the leaf and go; and the Sunday the twenty-fourth at about four, when he put his head in the door and looked at the four pages and did not come in. **He has carried a page nine years and in nine years has never once asked himself whether he was allowed to, and what he has looked at is whether anybody has noticed. He asked whether he had been carrying it right and the holder could not tell him. He said he is going to keep carrying it and gave the reason, that he is sixty-four and it is the only thing he has that is not in a house where it does not belong. He lost a day of a joiner's trade to a shed on this mole, about three marks, entered in his own book against the Thursday the twenty-first. He asked this yard for nothing and this yard offered him nothing. He was not thanked and did not ask.**
- **A woman of seventy-one of this harbor, whose house is on the north side of this town.** One visit up the hill, on Saturday the sixteenth, and one at about four on the Tuesday the twenty-sixth to take her page. **She came up the mole on foot, stood at the door for about a minute, said she was not answering a knock, and said that she had known since about half past seven that morning that she was going to answer a question about a night and had not let herself stop walking. She was not in the room when it was read and was never told about the reading and has no copy of it and does not want one. She is the third person in this batch who has told this yard what a page is and the only one of the three who had never been asked.**
- **A man of about thirty-four who sells lime and chalk out of a yard at the head of this dock, and has done since he was twenty-two.** Two occasions: Saturday the sixteenth with an empty barrow behind him and a sheet in a crate, and Saturday the thirtieth to collect it. **He is sixty pounds short that month and has not put that on anybody. He carried a sheet up a hill on nothing and said he was going to be asked about it at four houses that week. He said a page that is in a place is read by the people of that place, and that he had watched a page get read in a town it does not belong to and had not stopped it, and that he was one of the ones reading it. He took the sheet down the hill in his coat and not in the barrow, and said he did not have a reason for that that made any difference. He is not a villain, is not on a ladder, has no title, and is the whole of the cost of the batch's fourth record.**
- **A man of the second lay with a boat of about seventy tons**, who brought the first of the four up that hill in a piece of oilcloth with his pump and his man, who said nine words about it at the head of that dock, who had it in his locker for eleven days and would not be told what was in it, and who took it down the hill on the Tuesday the twenty-sixth and asked nothing about what had been said about it. **THE FIGURE ON THE PAGE IS: HE CAME UP ON THE EIGHTEENTH OF JANUARY WITH THE PUMP AND THE MAN AND THE PAGE, AND HE TOOK IT DOWN ON THE TWENTY-SIXTH. THE FIGURE OF *ELEVEN DAYS* IS HIS OWN AND IS ELEVEN DAYS IN A BOAT'S LOCKER FROM THE TUESDAY BOAT TO THE MONDAY HE BROUGHT IT UP.**
- **Two men of the first lay, unnamed, unasked.** They said a thing about this yard at the head of that dock on three days inside five weeks, the seventeenth and nineteenth of December past and Saturday the ninth of January instant, and **this batch made no fourth occasion of it and went up on none of the three, and the reason against all three lines is the reason of the seventeenth of December: a correction is the reason, and the reason does not go into a street.**
- **Ors Kest is in no chapter of this batch and in no room in it.** His page of his own went in on the tenth of December past and he said he was not going to do that twice inside a month without saying so out loud first, and it is inside a month, and so he was not asked and he is not in it. **HE IS STILL NOT A FRIEND OF THIS PARTY.**
- **Mara Venn is in no chapter of this batch as a person, is not in a room, is not cited, quoted, produced or asked again, and no letter of hers came up that hill in these twenty days. Her forty marks stand first after food and her six marks and two days stands as a price and not a debt.**
- **Bevin Rook is in no chapter of this batch as a person.** The three nots stand. Forty marks stands whole. The head of the third column keeps his hand. **THE THIRD COLUMN WAS NOT FILLED ON ANY DAY OF THIS BATCH AND NOBODY WAS APPOINTED TO IT. NOTHING WAS READ OUT OF IT IN IT. THE FIRST COLUMN WAS READ BACK ON THE TWENTY-SEVENTH AND FOUND TO BE A LINE OF CUSTODY, AND THE HEAD OF THE THIRD COLUMN IS THE THIRD OF THE FOUR PAGES, WHICH WAS READ AT THE TOP OF THE BENCH ON THE TWENTY-SIXTH. **THE EARLIER SENTENCE HERE READ *IT WAS READ TWICE, ON THE TWENTY-SEVENTH AND THE TWENTY-SIXTH*, WHICH NAMED A READ THAT DID NOT HAPPEN AND CONFLATED THE FIRST COLUMN WITH THE THIRD, AND IT IS WITHDRAWN.**
- **Alden Marr, sixty-one, at the far bench on one day of this batch, the first of February, from about ten until about four, and entered as not occupied on eighteen of the twenty days, and on neither brother going over on any of them.**
- **Captain Veyra Holt is not in this harbor, is not in a room, and her name is on no page of this batch. Halven Rook is not in a room and is not in this batch. Magister Ilya Serr is on no page of this batch at all. The man in a coat of an office in a city stays unnamed, did not come up that hill a second time in these twenty days, and the reason is on the page and is not a defect. The Court of Wreck Claims does not speak and sent nothing up that hill. The coast office said no sentence in these twenty days and was not given a third one. Ambrose Sell has not been up that hill since the twenty-eighth of October 2026 and is in no room in this batch. The four people of the Sill are not named as persons in this batch, their limit is quoted in this yard's own first column in Chapter 230, it stands, and the holder did not ask to have it lifted once in twenty days.**
- **THE FOUR WHO MAY NOT APPEAR IN A ROOM, AND DID NOT: MARA VENN, BEVIN ROOK, ALDEN MARR AS A PERSON RATHER THAN A BENCH, AND THE MAN IN A COAT. NO NEW ANTAGONIST, NO NEW INSTITUTION, NO NEW FINAL ENEMY, NO NAMED OFFICE THAT DID NOT EXIST IN VOLUME 04, AND NO NEW CHARACTER WITH A TITLE, A UNIFORM, A COMMISSION OR A MOTIVE OUTSIDE HER OWN TRADE'S WORDS. NO PERSON IN ANY OF THE TEN CHAPTERS HAS A TITLE, AND NO OFFICE SPOKE.**

### 7. The batch's ten cards, delivered, and the two devices it spent and the two it did not

1. **221 — where the four come from. PAID.** The two second-column lines read out and **the bare fact of the nine was already in that book and is not new in this volume**, and the chapter's work is that somebody reads the line and asks what the nine are. **The four arrive by four routes and the four routes are the chapter: shown, produced, ordinary traffic, and a boat's locker.** No record is opened and the chapter says why. The far bench not occupied on both days, no day of work on either. The cost is in the second column and it is the same act at a smaller size as Movement 1's refusal.
2. **222 — the first of the four, and what it is a record of. PAID.** The thirty-seventh Monday, bare, the cistern charged and walked on none, the first of five. A working day. **The first of the four is a page that is not a copy of anything and is simply the page a place has, and the ship's hand reads it and the holder does not read it for an hour and a quarter, and the chapter is the other one listening.** The read-back runs. The cost is a day of the ship's hand lost, in the second column, with no name in it.
3. **223 — the second, and the price of a Tuesday. PAID.** **The wage does not go in and the number of weeks fallen due is THIRTEEN, all thirteen in the same breath, and the reason is the reason of the twenty-ninth of December and is not improved on.** A working day on the Wednesday. **The second record disagrees with the first about a thing both of them saw, both are true, and the disagreement is the finding, and IT IS NOT RESOLVED ON THE PAGE AND WAS NOT RESOLVED ANYWHERE IN THIS BATCH.** The second of the four is quoted **in a woman's mouth, in pieces, and it is a line a woman of seventy-one can recite at sixty-two years' standing and did.**
4. **224 — the third, and the cost of a man whose trade is not the yard's. PAID.** **The cistern is charged on the rota day and walked on none, the second of five.** **The third record comes from a place four days up this coast and getting it here cost somebody a day of a trade, and the day is entered with a figure on it, being about three marks, in his own book and in this yard's first column and NOT in this yard's money, and it is not a cost paid twice and it is not any of the ten costs already paid in Movements 1 and 2.** The record is SHOWN and LENT and **NOT READ.**
5. **225 — the fourth, which is the ninth of the nine. PAID. NO ROOM, NO MARKET, NO CLERK, NO MAN WITH A SEAL, AND NO COMPACT CONFIRMED.** **The fourth of the four is the ninth of the nine and it is a record of an agreement and it carries a name, and THE NAME IS WRITTEN ONCE IN THE WHOLE OF VOLUME 05, IN CHAPTER 225, IN THE MOUTH OF THE SHEET.** It is a name of an agreement and not of a body, and it is not the name of any body, and it does not say that nine communities ever made one. **THE RECORD DOES NOT SAY THE AGREEMENT HELD, AND THE YARD IS NOT GOING TO SAY IT EITHER, AND THE NAME IS NOT WRITTEN IN THIS YARD'S BOOK AND IS REFERRED TO AFTERWARDS ONLY AS THE NAME AT THE HEAD OF THE FOURTH OF THE FOUR.**
6. **226 — the reading. PAID.** The thirty-eighth Monday, bare, the cistern charged and walked on none, the third of five. **THE FOUR ARE READ SIDE BY SIDE FROM ABOUT TWO UNTIL ABOUT FOUR ON THE MONDAY AFTERNOON, AT THE TOP OF THAT BENCH, IN THAT SHED, IN ABOUT TWO HOURS, BY TWO PEOPLE, AND THERE WAS NO CLERK IN THAT ROOM AND NO MAN WITH A SEAL IN THAT ROOM AND NO MARKET ANYWHERE NEAR IT. THE FOUR ARE INCOMPATIBLE AND ALL FOUR OF THEM ARE TRUE, AND THE INCOMPATIBILITY IS THE FINDING.** Three of the four are put side by side and a sentence that would settle the light is written four times in the holder's head and not put on the page. **PUTTING THEM SIDE BY SIDE PRODUCES A FIFTH THING THAT NONE OF THE FOUR SAYS: THERE IS NOT ONE DATE ON ANY OF THE FOUR, AND A PENCIL WAS OUT, AND FOUR DATES COULD HAVE BEEN INVENTED AND WOULD HAVE LOOKED RIGHT, AND NOTHING WAS PUT ON THE PAGE. THAT FIFTH THING IS ABOUT THE SHAPE OF THE FOUR AND IS NOT THE COMPACT AND IS NOT A CONCLUSION AND IS NOT AN ANSWER TO ANYTHING.** The wage does not go in on the Tuesday and the number of weeks fallen due is FOURTEEN, all fourteen in the same breath. Three pages go home.
7. **227 — the reversal. PAID.** The cistern charged on the Thursday and walked on none, the fourth of five. **THE YARD DISCOVERS THAT ITS OWN FIRST COLUMN IS A LINE OF CUSTODY WITH A NAMED PERSON AT THE END OF EVERY LINE, AND THAT THIS IS THE FIRST THING ABOUT ITS OWN METHOD IT HAS NOT BEEN ABLE TO SEE BECAUSE IT WAS INSIDE IT.** **THE FOUR NAMELESS LINES ABOVE THE NAMED LINE OF THE TWENTIETH OF JULY ARE STILL FOUR, ARE STILL NAMELESS, AND ARE NOT STRUCK OUT, AND A REQUEST TO STRIKE A LINE OUT OF A COLUMN IS REFUSED IN THE SAME WORDS IT IS REFUSED FOR A LINE IN ANY COLUMN, AND THE REQUEST WAS MADE AND THE WORDS WERE SAID.** **A PARTY THAT HAS SPENT FOUR VOLUMES INSISTING THAT A RECORD A MAN CAN CHECK IS THE ONLY KIND WORTH HAVING ARRIVES, IN ONE WEEK, AT A RECORD NOBODY CAN CHECK AND CANNOT SAY WHETHER THAT IS BETTER OR WORSE, AND GOES TO A COPYIST OF FIFTY-EIGHT WITH A COUNTER OFF THE FISH MARKET TO ASK, AND SHE IS THE ONLY PERSON IN THIS HARBOR WHO CAN PRICE THE SHAPE OF A PAGE, AND SHE IS NOT TOLD WHAT A SECOND COLUMN IS.** A penny goes out, the first money this yard has spent in a month, for a sheet of paper and nothing else.
8. **228 — the ninth-line mark, and the four places that are not the nine. PAID. LOCK L16 CLOSES IN THIS VOLUME AND CLOSES HERE, AND ONLY AS A FACT.** **A BUILDER'S MARK OF A PRE-ACCORD CONSTRUCTION, NOT A CLAIM SEAL AND NOT A MARK OF CONSENT, AND NO OFFICE IN THIS COUNTRY CAN READ IT, AND THIS PARTY HAS COUNTED A ROW OF NINE ONCE AND IS NOT GOING TO COUNT IT TWICE, AND THE CHAPTER MAY NOT SAY WHAT IT IS FOR AND DID NOT.** **THE NINE FASTENINGS IN ABOUT SEVEN FEET OF EACH OF THE SIX JOINTS ARE NOT A MARK OF NINE JOINED LINES; THE NINE PLACES IN SIX BOOKS ARE NOT THE NINE COMMUNITIES; THE NINE RECORDS OF NINE COMMUNITIES ARE NOT THE NINE PLACES IN SIX BOOKS; AND NEITHER MAY BE CONVERTED INTO EITHER, AND THE CHAPTER MAKES THE LAST OF THOSE FOUR A SENTENCE IN A CHARACTER'S MOUTH: the point with the light is on the list as a place and the light in the second of the four pages has nothing to do with it.** **THE OTHER FIVE OF THE NINE ARE NAMED IN THE YARD'S OWN BOOK AS PLACES AND NOT AS RECORDS, AND THE NAMING OF THE OTHER FIVE IS THE SECOND HALF OF THE CHAPTER, AND THEY ARE THIS HARBOR'S OWN WEIR, THE POINT WITH THE LIGHT, THE NEXT TOWN DOWN THIS COAST, THE HARD AT ASHTIDE AND LOWFEN.** The fourth of the four goes down that hill in the inside of a man's coat and the bench under the pump is bare for the first time since the ninth of December.
9. **229 — the cost, and the turn. PAID.** The thirty-ninth Monday, bare, **the cistern charged on the rota day and walked on none, and that is the fifth and last charge this batch touches.** **A COST FALLS ON SOMEBODY WHO IS NOT IN THIS YARD AND IT IS NOT ANY OF THE TEN ALREADY PAID, AND THE CHAPTER SAYS WHICH SHAPE IT IS: NOT A PERSON WHO HAS READ A PAGE AND CANNOT UNREAD IT, BUT A SHEET THAT HAS BEEN ON A BENCH IN THIS TOWN FOR FOURTEEN DAYS AND HAS GONE HOME DOWN THAT COAST IN THE INSIDE OF A MAN'S COAT, AND FOUR PEOPLE ARE GOING TO BE ASKED ABOUT IT BY THE MAN WHO SOLD THE LIME AND NOT ONE OF THEM BY THIS PARTY.** **The corner of the sheet and a half came off in the ship's hand while the five pieces of paper were laid out to look for one word, and cannot be put back, and the reason she gave on the fourteenth of January was true and was not the reason.** **AND THE TURN: the record-keeping this yard has been demanding of everybody else was once somebody's ordinary practice, and the practice had a name, and the name is on one sheet in this country that this yard has ever been shown and is on none of the five pieces of paper this yard holds, and the holder is not going to say that that is a fact about the world, because it is a fact about this yard's drawer.** Six centuries is the age of the practice and three hundred years is the age of an office and the two are not put in one sentence.
10. **230 — the batch closes. PAID. NEITHER OF THESE TWO DAYS IS A ROTA DAY AND NO CISTERN IS CHARGED IN THIS CHAPTER, WHICH IS NOT A FAULT AND IS THE SHAPE OF THE BATCH'S LAST PAGE.** **The wage is not paid and the number of weeks fallen due stands at FIFTEEN, all fifteen in the same breath.** A working day, the last day of work this batch books. The read-back runs. **A QUESTION IS LEFT STANDING THAT THIS BATCH DOES NOT ANSWER, IN THE SECOND COLUMN WITH A REASON AGAINST THE LINE: WHAT IS A COPY, and not what it is worth.** **A COST IS PAID, and it is the printer: this yard has the answer to Jonas Peake's one question in a drawer and is not going to send it, and the reason is in the first column because a man in this town can get on the coach and ask him.** **THE BATCH'S LAST LINE IS A FACT AND NOT A RESOLUTION, IT IS CHECKABLE BY ANY MAN WHO CAN GET OFF A MOLE, AND NOBODY IN THAT SHED IMPROVED ON IT.** **The writ runs to midnight on the first of March and this yard is a party of one and a half until that day, and there are twenty-five days between the third of February and the first of March, and that figure is a figure and not a plan.**

**THE READ-BACK — the day's entries read back from the top of the bench by the ship's hand and read back after her by the holder, nobody else in that shed — RAN IN FOUR OF THE TEN CHAPTERS AND THE HOUSE'S OWN PLAIN-STRING TEST FOR *read it back* OR *read back after her* RETURNS THE SAME FOUR: 222, 227, 229 AND 230.** All four are the shed-evening form. **THE CHART IS: 221 0 · 222 1 · 223 0 · 224 0 · 225 0 · 226 0 · 227 1 · 228 0 · 229 1 · 230 1. FOUR CHAPTERS, FOUR, AND THE STRING TEST AND THE COUNT AGREE.** 225's is deliberately absent and the chapter gives the reason: two days of a fortnight that this yard spent on somebody else's page are not a night in which the yard's own day can be read back by two people, and the fourth of the four is a sheet and not a day. 223's and 224's and 226's and 228's are absent and three of those four chapters say why on the page or do not need to.

**THE READ-OUT DID NOT RUN IN THIS BATCH AND ITS ALLOWANCE WAS NOT USED, AND THE REASON IS GIVEN AT § 1 AND IS A CHOICE. THE BENCH READING OF CHAPTER 226 IS NOT THE READ-OUT, IS NOT COVERED BY ITS ALLOWANCE, AND RAN LONG, AND § 1 IS THE RECORD OF THAT.**

1. **It may not be used to answer the new-volume question.** The question a man of the first lay put in a market in this harbor on the second of December is referred to nowhere in this batch and asked by nobody in it, **and no office answers it, no document answers it, no compact is named as an answer, and it is not confirmed.** A case-insensitive search of the ten chapters for *Orison*, *Quietening*, *Crown Seal*, *Returning Memory*, *network*, *Mara Venn*, *Bevin*, *Captain Veyra*, *Halven Rook*, *Ilya Serr* and *Ambrose Sell* returns nothing.
2. **It may not be used to confirm the compact, to say that the nine communities made one body, or to say that the agreement held.** **The four records are incompatible and all four of them are true, and that is the finding. A fifth thing about the shape of the four was produced by putting them side by side, and it is a fact about four pages and not a conclusion, and the yard entered that it is not the compact and did not say what it means.** A search of the ten chapters for *compact* returns nothing; the word on the page is **agreement**.
3. **It may not be used to write the name of the compact again.** **THE NAME IS *THE NINE HARBORS*, IT IS WRITTEN ONCE, AT `chapter-0225.md` LINE 27, IN THE MOUTH OF THE SHEET, AND A CASE-INSENSITIVE SEARCH OF ALL TEN CHAPTERS RETURNS EXACTLY ONE HIT.** Everywhere else in the volume, including the rest of Chapter 225, the thing is called **the name at the head of the fourth of the four**. **A LATER CHAPTER MAY NOT WRITE IT OUT AGAIN AND MAY NOT PUT IT IN A PERSON'S MOUTH, AND MAY NOT PUT IT ON A WALL, WHICH IS ALSO FORBIDDEN BY LOCK L33.**
4. **It may not be used to prove who altered the manifest, or to name a person, an office that agreed to a removal as a body that decided anything, or a hand.** The discrepancy was not used, not closed and not restated. **THE COMPARTMENT IS NOT NAMED, THE THREE GANNET DOCUMENTS ARE STILL THREE, NO STEP OF THE COMPARTMENT'S FINDING IS RESTATED, THE ITEM IS NOT A FOURTH ITEM, NO DIGIT OF ANY OF THE THREE NUMBERS IS ON ANY PAGE OF THIS BATCH, AND THE SEALED CASE'S POSITION IS NOT STATED OR IMPLIED.**
5. **It may not be used to move the Second Bell eligibility onto the writ, to say the court refused him anything, to say the court found against him, to say the writ took it, to say he has sat the examination since September 2025, or to apply for it.** **THE WRIT'S FOURTH DAY OF JANUARY FELL BEFORE THIS BATCH AND NOTHING HAPPENED, AND THIS PARTY ASKED NO OFFICE FOR ANYTHING IN AID OF IT, SENT NOTHING TO A CITY, DID NOT WRITE TO A MAN IN A COAT, AND HAS NOT BEEN TO THE COUNTER OF THAT CIRCUIT OFFICE SINCE THE TWENTY-FOURTH OF NOVEMBER 2026, AND NONE OF THAT CHANGED IN THESE TWENTY DAYS.**
6. **It may not be used to name the condition.** It is named nowhere in this batch. **The body is charged and the name is not written: a night of Sunday the seventeenth of January was lost to it, the day is entered as a day this yard did not work in the second column with a reason against the line and no name in it. The four lines above the named line of the twentieth of July 2026 are still four, are still nameless, are not struck out, and a request to strike a line out of a column was refused in the same words it is refused for a line in any column.**
7. **It may not be used to take a power stage.** No stage of any kind is taken. The Faultreader is not re-taken, improved or named, **and the word is on no page of these ten chapters. THE BELLWRIGHT STAGE IS NOT TAKEN, IS NOT NAMED, AND IS NOT DISCHARGED IN ANY OF ITS THREE COSTS: the book of hours stands at sixteen lines and is not extended, and the nineteen lines of the thirtieth of December are a list of materials and not a stage, and a thing on the water is entered as a bill and not as an instrument, and this yard has not got a hand to go and look at one. NO BUOY WENT INTO ANY WATER AND NO KEEPLIGHT WAS EXTENDED.** The word *seam* on a page of this batch is the mole's own second and fifth seams and a day of work at a seam, and is not the perception.
8. **It may not be used to pay any item on the labor list**, to reduce any figure, to re-write the chandler's note or advance any of its three counts, to pay the bellwright, to pay the seven pence, to pay the eight shillings and tenpence, to fill or appoint anybody to the third column, to scratch the boy's hand out of the head of it, to name or send for the man of Ashtide, to ask the bellwright in a shed, to print a digit of anything he said on the second of July, or to open the chest.
9. **It may not be used to reach the plate at the fifth seam, to close the plate note, to write a better letter about it, to open the case of five bells by argument, by right or by a seal, to ask the four of the Sill to take their line off, to measure or advance the delayed note or to write it down with a date against it, to look at the Kettle, to decide the coast road, or to call the coast road anything.**

THE FINAL CHAPTER IMAGE, WHICH INCLUDES A SHEET GOING UP ON A WALL IN A TOWN FOUR DAYS UP THIS COAST, IS THE VOLUME'S AND NOT THIS BATCH'S, AND NO CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH PRE-CUTS IT.**

A page that another person has read out in a doorway is a page, a form is a form, a rota is a rota, a list of nine places is a list of nine places, and a letter is a letter. **NO CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH MAY BE SHOWN A DOCUMENT BY A NARRATION THAT OPENS IT; EVERY ONE OF THE FOUR RECORDS ARRIVES AS A THING FOUR PEOPLE HAVE PUT IN FRONT OF TWO PEOPLE, AND A PERSON WHO HAD NEVER SEEN THE FOURTH WAS NOT TOLD WHAT WAS ON IT.**
14. **It may not be used to fuse the four records with one another, or with any of the five pieces of paper, or with the new-volume question.** They are four records and five papers and are kept apart on the page, and the yard's refusal to make a boat of about sixty tons into one boat is on the page in two places.

The reason was entered once, on the twenty-ninth of December, and was not improved on and was not said again.**

5. **A DAY OF A JOINER'S TRADE AT ABOUT THREE MARKS, entered by the man in his own book against Thursday the twenty-first of January and entered by this yard in its first column because a man in this town can go and ask him, and entered as NOT in this yard's money and not going to be.**
6. **A MAN OF SIXTY-FOUR WHO WAS MADE THE REASON THERE WERE FOUR PAGES ON A BENCH IN THIS HARBOR AND DOES NOT KNOW IT, and who is going to be asked about it at his own house by a woman of sixty who is his aunt, and who is going to carry that page four days up this coast in the same book on Monday anyway. **NO MILEAGE FOR THE JOINER IS STATED ON THE PAGE AND NONE IS IN THIS FILE: HIS HOUSE IS *A PLACE FOUR DAYS UP THIS COAST*, WHICH IS WHAT CHAPTER 221 AND CHAPTER 224 GIVE. THE FIGURE OF NINE HUNDRED MILES IS WITHDRAWN. THE ONLY MILEAGE ON THE PAGE IN THIS BATCH IS *CARRIED FOUR HUNDRED MILES*, WHICH IS THE FIRST OF THE FOUR, OUT OF A BOAT'S LOCKER, IN CHAPTER 222.**
7. **A MAN OF THIRTY-FOUR WHO CARRIED A SHEET UP A HILL ON NOTHING AND IS SIXTY POUNDS SHORT IN A MONTH HE HAS NOT PUT ON ANYBODY, and who took it down the hill in his coat and not in his barrow, and who has watched a page get read in a town it does not belong to and did not stop it and was one of the ones reading it.**
8. **A SHEET AND A HALF, WHICH CAME UP THAT HILL ON FOOT ON THE NINTH OF DECEMBER PAST AND SAT ON A BENCH UNDER A PUMP FOR FIFTY-THREE DAYS, AND CAME APART IN THE SHIPWRIGHT'S HAND ON SUNDAY THE THIRTY-FIRST OF JANUARY ALONG THE FOLD THAT HAD BEEN GOING SOFT SINCE THE FOURTEENTH, AND CANNOT BE PUT BACK, AND CANNOT BE BOUGHT, AND THERE IS NOWHERE ON THIS COAST A MAN CAN BUY A SHEET OF PAPER WITH AN OFFICE'S NAME AT THE FOOT OF IT THAT NOBODY SENT HERE.**
9. **THE FOURTH OF THE FOUR WAS ON A BENCH IN THIS TOWN FOR FOURTEEN DAYS AND WENT HOME DOWN THAT COAST IN THE INSIDE OF A MAN'S COAT TO A PLACE TWO DAYS DOWN IT, and four people are going to be asked about it this week, and not one of them by this yard, and not one of the four is going to be told what two people said out loud on a Monday afternoon about a light on a point.** **THE EARLIER FORM OF THIS COST — *A PAGE THAT WAS IN A SHED IN ANOTHER TOWN FOR NINE DAYS* AND *FOUR PEOPLE WHO KEEP THAT PLACE WHO ARE GOING TO BE TOLD* — IS WITHDRAWN ON THREE COUNTS AND IS REPLACED BY WHAT CHAPTER 229 AND CHAPTER 228 SAY: THE SHEET WAS IN A SHED IN **THIS** TOWN AND NOT IN ANOTHER, AND THE OTHER TOWN IS WHERE IT BELONGS; IT WAS THERE FOURTEEN DAYS, FROM THE SIXTEENTH OF JANUARY TO THE THIRTIETH, AND NOT NINE; AND NOBODY IN THIS PARTY IS TELLING ANYBODY ANYTHING, THE FOUR ARE THE LIME MAN'S OWN CHALK CUSTOMERS AND THEY ARE GOING TO BE **ASKED** ABOUT THE SHEET BY HIM, AS HE SAID ON THE SIXTEENTH, AND CHAPTER 228 STANDS THAT THIS YARD HAS NOT WRITTEN TO A SINGLE ONE OF THE NINE AND HAS ASKED A SINGLE ONE OF THEM NOTHING.** The yard is not writing to them, is not sending anybody, and is not going to put a word into the ear of the man who is going to ask them, and the reason is the reason of the fourth of October past.
10. **A COPY OF THE FOURTH OF THE FOUR, WHICH THE YARD WOULD GIVE A YEAR FOR AND IS NOT GOING TO HAVE, because a copy of a page would have to be got from a place two hundred yards off the water by a woman who is seventy-one or bought at a counter off the fish market, and the reason it is not going to happen is not the money and is the fourth of the four.**
11. **THE PRINTER'S QUESTION OF THE TWENTIETH OF DECEMBER, UNANSWERED, AND THIS YARD HAS THE ANSWER IN A DRAWER AND IS NOT GOING TO SEND IT, because a printer in a town of about two thousand keeps a list of everything that comes into his shop that anybody means to keep, and a man with a book is a man this party would have to be able to lie to in four years.** Six weeks old and unanswered in both directions and this yard has not written.
12. **THE FOUR NAMES AND NO FIFTH, THE OUTER MARKS, AND TWENTY-FIVE DAYS.** The forty marks twice, neither reduced and neither paid; the third column unfilled and unappointed; the man of Ashtide's three marks unmoved and unasked about; the bellwright's eight marks and a day of a boat unargued and his chest unopened; the eight shillings and tenpence; the seven pence; the thirty-one on the chandler's note not re-written and not said out loud in eight weeks.
13. **A WORKING HARBOR POORER ON THE THIRD OF FEBRUARY THAN IT WAS ON THE FIFTEENTH OF JANUARY, AND THE CISTERN WALKED ON NONE OF FIVE CHARGES, AND NOTHING THIS YARD DID IN THREE WEEKS HAS MADE ANYTHING BETTER, AND NO FIGURE IN THIS HARBOR IS THE PRICE OF ANY OF IT.**

### 11. The shape of the batch, stated on the batch's own face

**THIS BATCH IS A READING MOVEMENT AND IT IS THE MIDPOINT OF VOLUME 05, AND IT HAS NO ACTION CHAPTER, NO FIGHT, NO UNDERWATER SCENE, NO DIVE, NO FINDING, NO BUOY IN THE WATER AND NO POWER STAGE. FIVE DAYS WERE WORKED AT THE FACE OF THE SECOND SEAM, ALL ON HIRERS' OWN ACCOUNTS, ALL WITH NOBODY IN THE WATER, AND EVERY ONE OF THE FIVE CAME UP THAT HILL BECAUSE A MAN BROUGHT A PUMP UP IT. FOUR THINGS CAME UP THAT HILL THAT DO NOT BELONG TO THIS YARD AND THREE OF THEM HAVE GONE BACK DOWN IT, AND THE FOURTH WENT DOWN IN THE INSIDE OF A MAN'S COAT, AND THE FIFTH THING THAT CAME OUT OF THEM IS THAT NONE OF THE FOUR CARRIES A DATE.** The alternation of pressure types is deliberate and is in the order a discovery and four routes, a working day and a document, a political day and a cost, character conflict and a cost, a discovery, an institutional reading, character conflict and a discovery, a working day and a discovery, political and a cost and a turn, and a working day and a question left standing. **The batch's discovery is in Chapter 222, that a page records where the person was standing, and it was said out loud by a woman of seventy-one in her own front room. The batch's reversal is in Chapter 227, that this yard's own first column is a line of custody with a name at the end of every line and four gaps in it, and that a request to strike those four out was refused in the same words it is refused for a line in any column. And the batch's turn is Chapter 229's, in a shed on the first of February, and it is that the record-keeping this yard has been demanding of everybody else was once somebody's ordinary practice, and that the practice had a name, and that the name is on one sheet in this country that this yard has ever been shown.**

**THE BATCH'S ONE WORKING RULE, WHICH IS THE MOVEMENT'S AND IS NOT INVENTED IN IT: A PAGE IS NOT READ ON THE DAY IT ARRIVES, AND A PAGE IS A RECORD OF WHERE THE PERSON WAS STANDING WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN, AND NEITHER OF THOSE TWO SENTENCES IS A CONCLUSION, A COMPACT, OR AN ANSWER TO ANYTHING.**
